article.articleHeadline: 內地流感進入流行季　國家疾控局籲接種疫苗
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza in Mainland China Enters Flu Season; National CDC Urges Vaccination.
article.articleSummary: Influenza has entered the seasonal peak in Mainland China, with acute respiratory infections rising as winter approaches and heightened attention to influenza cases in infants and young children. Dengue fever and chikungunya remain risks from imported cases, and norovirus outbreaks may occur in crowded venues. The National CDC spokesperson announced free and supportive influenza vaccination policies for key groups: the elderly and young children in rural areas; insured workers and their dependents; and workers in new forms of employment. Local authorities are expanding weekend and targeted vaccination sessions and urging timely bookings. With cold, dry winter weather potentially lowering immunity, health authorities advocate good hygiene, regular routines, moderate exercise, appropriate clothing, frequent handwashing, ventilation, and safe food practices. High-risk groups—infants, the elderly, pregnant women, and people with chronic diseases—should monitor health and seek medical care promptly if unwell.

article.articleHeadline: 流感已进入流行季；赛诺菲拟410亿美元现金收购Insmed
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The flu season has begun; Sanofi to acquire Insmed for $41 billion in cash.
article.articleSummary: Influenza has entered the seasonal outbreak in China, with the National CDC urging timely vaccination and rolling out programs that subsidize or provide free vaccines for rural residents, insured workers, and other groups; weekend and vaccination sessions are promoted to improve coverage. In health innovation, the UK launched an AI-assisted breast cancer screening trial in Cambridge to assess earlier detection and alleviate radiologist workload. In biopharma news, Sanofi agreed to pay $41 billion in cash to acquire Insmed, aiming to close in early 2027 and lift EPS by 2028. In China, Shanghai Pharma’s systemic lupus erythematosus antibody-drug conjugate B024 won clinical-trial approval; Lizhu Group’s tripartite influenza recombinant protein vaccine (LZSN2401) began clinical trials for older adults; ST Renfu’s oseltamivir phosphate dry suspension received a drug-registration certificate for treatment of influenza A/B and prevention in children aged 1 year and older. The week underscores ongoing vaccine development and public health measures.

article.articleHeadline: Workers in high-risk jobs to receive shots against rabies in Tamil Nadu
article.articleSummary: Rabies PrEP rollout in Tamil Nadu targets high-risk workers across 38 districts under SAPRE Vision 2030. The government has sanctioned ₹2.22 crore, funded by the National Health Mission, Tamil Nadu, to immunize sanitation workers, local-body dog catchers/animal handlers, and Animal Husbandry Department personnel involved in dog-catching, veterinary and para-veterinary activities. Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis aims to bolster rabies elimination by protecting those with sustained exposure to dogs and potentially rabid animals. Eligibility follows National Guidelines on Rabies Prophylaxis based on occupational risk. Preliminary beneficiary estimates include 1,29,009–1,21,844 local body sanitation workers; 3,324 animal handlers/dog catchers; and 3,841 Animal Husbandry staff. Implementation will occur through Primary Health Centres, Urban PHCs, government hospitals, and medical college hospitals; local bodies and the Animal Husbandry Department will identify beneficiaries and mobilize participation.

article.articleHeadline: Pernambuco confirma foco de raiva em vaca e determina vacinação em oito municípios; veja quais
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pernambuco confirms a rabies focus in cattle and mandates vaccination in eight municipalities; see which ones.
article.articleSummary: Rabies focus in herbivores confirmed in Pernambuco, Brazil, after a dairy cow in São João, Agreste, tested positive. ADAGRO confirmed the case; direct immunofluorescence yielded a positive result on Nov 17, with the LABVET sample from Goiânia (GO). The unvaccinated cow showed illness starting Oct 23 and died Oct 25; investigation noted a bat bite on a calf two months earlier. A 12 km surveillance radius covers eight municipalities: São João, Angelim, Calçado, Canhotinho, Jupi, Jucati, Lajedo and Garanhuns. Vaccination of bovines, buffaloes, sheep, goats, and horses aged three months or older is mandatory within the zone, with a Feb 15, 2027 deadline. Per Portaria ADAGRO 068/2025, a booster is given 30 days after the first dose and vaccination must be declared to ADAGRO within 30 days, with vaccine documentation.

article.articleHeadline: National Study Finds Widespread Bacterial Contamination Across Indonesian
article.articleSummary: Indonesia’s 2020 SKAM-RT study analyzed 19,900 households across 34 provinces to establish a baseline for drinking-water quality. Escherichia coli was detected in 67.8% of collection points, with only 32.2% meeting WHO safety benchmarks (<1 CFU/100 mL); 23.5% were medium risk, 24.5% high risk, and 19.9% very high contamination (>100 CFU/100 mL). Point-of-use samples showed no detectable E. coli in 72.9% of cases; among the 27.1% with bacteria, 16.1% had 1–10 CFU/mL, 7.9% 11–100 CFU/mL, and 3.1% >100 CFU/mL. Self-supplied sources (39.5% of collection points) had nearly 70% contamination, with boreholes faring best among these and open surface water worst. Largest regional samples came from East Java, Central Java, and West Java. Context notes link unsafe water to pediatric diarrhea and stunting, within Indonesia’s SDG6.1 framework and a 2021 safely managed-water target of 11.8%.

article.articleHeadline: تحالف عالمي يعتزم توفير 1.5 مليون جرعة من لقاح تجريبي ضد إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A global alliance plans to supply 1.5 million doses of an experimental Ebola vaccine.
article.articleSummary: GAVI plans to purchase up to 1.5 million doses of an experimental Ebola vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain that is driving the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak, contingent on confirmed safety and efficacy. The vaccine, developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, is in clinical trials in the DRC, where there are no licensed vaccines or treatments for this strain. The outbreak has killed more than 5,700 people to date. About $40 million is earmarked to support vaccine development, with calls for additional funding and accelerated distribution protocols if efficacy is demonstrated. Sana Nishtar, GAVI’s CEO, stressed that access to the experimental vaccine requires regulatory clearance and clear monitoring guidelines, and she hopes the World Health Organization will expedite process. The plan depends on forthcoming trial results from the DRC.

article.articleHeadline: Thai DDC Reveals That There Were 13,225 New COVID-19 cases Between October 25th-November 23rd
article.articleSummary: Thailand's Department of Disease Control reports 13,225 new COVID-19 cases nationwide between October 25 and November 23, 2026, raising the 2026 cumulative total to 221,356. From January 1 to November 23, 2026, Thailand recorded 222,464 COVID-19 cases, about 441 daily. There have been 46 COVID-19–related deaths this year. The figures were presented at a November 24 press briefing by DDC spokespersons Dr. Jurai Wongsawat and Dr. Weerawat Manosuthi. The surveillance data did not include hospitalization numbers or variant distributions, and officials cautioned that official counts may underestimate the true burden due to under-testing of mild or asymptomatic cases. COVID-19 remains a persistent public health concern in Thailand, with continued emphasis on testing access, indoor ventilation, and public awareness to protect vulnerable groups.

article.articleHeadline: Bộ Y tế cung cấp thông tin mới về bệnh COVID-19
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health provides new information about COVID-19.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19: Vietnam’s Ministry of Health notes WHO’s preliminary risk assessment for SARS-CoV-2 PJ.2.1, an Omicron JN.1 subline, placed under monitoring. There is currently no evidence that PJ.2.1 causes more severe disease or increases hospitalization, ICU admission, or death; data remain insufficient to confirm higher transmissibility or immune escape. PJ.2.1 has been detected more in sequencing data from some countries, mainly in the Americas—Canada and the United States—but sampling/reporting differences may bias this signal. WHO regards global health risk from PJ.2.1 as low with low confidence. Vietnam emphasizes continued vigilance rather than alarm; seasonally, winter–spring and rising gatherings could raise respiratory disease transmission, including COVID-19. Preventive measures urged: correct masking in healthcare settings, public transport, crowded or poorly ventilated spaces; regular hand hygiene; cover coughs; ventilate indoor spaces; seek medical care promptly if symptoms appear; avoid self-medication; high-risk individuals should take extra precautions. The department will keep monitoring and update guidance.

article.articleHeadline: PU scientists patent quantum dot technology to detect bacteria in drinking water
article.articleSummary: Chandigarh-based Panjab University researchers have patented a quantum dot–based technology to detect Escherichia coli in drinking water, a GI and water-borne pathogen. The University Institute of Pharmaceutical Sciences team, led by Dr. Gurpal Singh with Prof. Bhupinder Singh Bhoop, uses a specially treated glass surface to capture bacteria and quantum dots to emit fluorescent signals, enabling detection of E. coli that cannot be seen, smelled, or tasted. The invention, titled Selective capturing and detection of pathogens on glass matrix using affinity moiety coupled quantum dots, received Indian patent 610483 on Nov 20, with filing on Feb 14, 2019. It could underpin a portable, user-friendly water-testing kit and be adapted for other pathogens by changing recognition molecules. Applications include drinking-water surveillance and public-health monitoring in areas with limited testing, though deployment requires further development.

article.articleHeadline: Pemkot Pontianak intensifkan penanganan DBD
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pontianak City Government intensifies dengue fever response
article.articleSummary: As of 25 November 2026, Pontianak, West Kalimantan, Indonesia, authorities report rising dengue fever (DBD) and chikungunya cases with more hospitalizations. Mayor Edi Rusdi Kamtono directs Dinas Kesehatan to intensify on-the-ground response, including expansive fogging across all kelurahan, while stressing that mosquito breeding sites must be eliminated by the community. The shift from dry to rainy season is increasing standing water in discarded cans, tires, jars, and other containers that serve as mosquito habitats. In addition to fogging, residents are urged to participate in 3M Plus: drain and scrub water containers, cover water storage, and recycle or discard items that collect water. Abate larvicide powder is available at local Puskesmas with ID verification. Regular environmental checks (gutters, plant stands, yard corners) are planned. People with fever, joint pain, or symptoms suggestive of DBD or chikungunya should seek medical evaluation promptly.

article.articleHeadline: ไข้สูง ระวัง 'ไข้หวัดใหญ่ในเด็ก' เสี่ยงลุกลามถึงปอดอักเสบ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: High fever: beware of 'influenza in children'—risk of progressing to pneumonia.
article.articleSummary: Influenza poses a higher risk of pneumonia and other severe complications in children under 5, the elderly, pregnant women, and those with chronic diseases in Thailand. Dr. Muangphrae Jantanakul, a pediatric pulmonologist at Rama IX Hospital, notes influenza spreads rapidly via droplets and can cause pneumonia, myocarditis, or encephalitis, potentially fatal without timely care. Illness onset is abrupt, 1–4 days after exposure, with fever ≥38°C, chills, headache, myalgia, fatigue, cough, sore throat, and congestion; some children experience nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Distinguish from the common cold: high fever lasting 2–3 days, lethargy, reduced appetite, rapid breathing or chest retractions require prompt medical evaluation, especially around days 3–5 when complications may arise. Prevention includes hygiene, masks, and annual vaccination. Thailand offers injectable inactivated vaccine (from 6 months) and nasal spray live attenuated; nasal spray is not suitable for pregnant women, immunocompromised, regular aspirin users, or poorly controlled asthma—consult a physician. Vaccination reduces severity and mortality, though not infection. For more information, Rama IX Hospital: 1270 or Line: @praram9hospital.

article.articleHeadline: Evaluasi Penanganan KLB Difteri, Wabup Lom Lom Minta Respons Diperkuat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Evaluation of the Diphtheria Outbreak Handling, Lom Lom Deputy Regent Calls for a Strengthened Response
article.articleSummary: Thirteen diphtheria cases across six districts of Deli Serdang Regency, Indonesia, were recorded by November 2026, triggering a focused evaluation of outbreak response. An Intra-Action Review (IAR) was held in Lubuk Pakam on 24–25 November 2026 to assess epidemiological investigations, contact tracing, chemoprophylaxis, and Outbreak Response Immunization (ORI), with ORI rounds surpassing 95% coverage though new cases persisted into early November. Deli Serdang had re-established the diphtheria outbreak status on 11 June 2026. Key recommendations emphasize earlier detection and case management, readiness of health facilities (isolation capacity, antibiotics, Anti-Diphtheria Serum ADS), and rigorous monitoring and treatment adherence for all contacts to prevent further transmission. Attention to cross-sector collaboration is urged to counter misinformation and vaccine hesitancy; roles for camats, village heads, religious and community leaders, health workers, and Posyandu cadres are highlighted to deliver accurate, clear messaging. Keywords: vaccination, outbreak, public health measures.

article.articleHeadline: Post-Exposure Rabies Prophylaxis Clears Viral RNA and Maintains Protective
article.articleSummary: Twenty immunologically naïve adults with category III dog bites were enrolled at an anti-rabies clinic of a northern Indian tertiary hospital (Government Medical College, Patiala, Punjab). Post-exposure prophylaxis comprised CHIRORAB vaccine (batch R25047D) with Premi-RAB immunoglobulin (batch RAB-091), administered per protocol with allowable +/-2 days for vaccination. Between 48 and 120 days post-exposure, real-time RT-PCR detected zero circulating rabies viral RNA in all participants; serology by ELISA showed protective titers above 0.5 IU/mL in every subject, indicating durable humoral immunity. Baseline testing confirmed seronegativity. The cohort included 20 individuals: 50% aged 18–30, 30% 31–45, 20% 46–60; 70% male; 60% urban, 40% rural; 90% dog bites, 85% unprovoked, 65% lower-limb injuries. The findings question the necessity of the one-year donor deferral after anti-rabies treatment and support reassessment of current transfusion-safety guidelines.

article.articleHeadline: موذی مرض ایبولا سے نبرد آزما عالمی ادارہ صحت کی طبی ٹیم کو تین دن بعد کانگو کے اسپتال نکال لیا گیا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The World Health Organization's medical team, battling the deadly Ebola disease, was withdrawn from a hospital in Congo after three days.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak, armed clashes in Ituri province's Akwi area forced the World Health Organization and local health staff to shelter inside a hospital for more than three days before evacuation to safety. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said staff from WHO, Congo's Ministry of Health, and partner agencies were trapped as fighting intensified, with teams temporarily relocated. This outbreak, described by WHO as the worst in the country's history, has reached 11,762 reported cases, with 5,775 deaths officially confirmed. Since October, violence has surged, severely hampering response efforts. The outbreak began in May, and the Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment currently available.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱と闘っていたWHOの医療チームが、コンゴの病院から3日後に撤収された
triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ流行は過去最悪規模（患者11,762人、死者5,775人）で、武装衝突によりWHO職員が病院に足止めされるなど対応が著しく阻害されており、IHR基準2つ以上・WPRO基準も複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にGhanaが含まれるが、記事サマリーではGhanaへの言及がないため除外。武装紛争による対応阻害がリスクをさらに高めている点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Bangladesh measles outbreak claims 1,361 lives: Should India be worried about cross-border spread?
article.articleSummary: Bangladesh’s 2026 measles outbreak has caused 1,361 deaths (105 confirmed, 1,256 suspected) with 26,300 confirmed cases and 2,59,190 suspected in total; 1,283 new suspected cases were reported, and nine suspected deaths occurred in the 24 hours to Tuesday morning. The outbreak is linked to immunity gaps, nationwide stockouts of measles-rubella vaccines in 2024–2025, gaps in routine immunisation, and no nationwide supplementary vaccination campaigns since 2020. WHO assesses national risk as high and cross-border transmission risk as considerable, given population movement and vaccination gaps. Nearby India faces elevated concern due to proximity and shared borders; WHO notes travel hubs Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet, and Cox’s Bazar, with land crossings near Jashore and Chapainawabganj as relevant routes. India’s 2025 vaccination coverage stood at 98% for the first dose and 95% for the second dose, though local gaps persist. Measles transmits via air/respiratory droplets; symptoms include fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, white mouth spots, and rash, typically 10–14 days post-exposure. The report cautions against assuming an immediate nationwide threat in India.

article.articleHeadline: Panjab University Scientists Secure Patent For Quantum Dot Technology To Detect Harmful Bacteria In Water
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-25, Panjab University in Chandigarh has secured patent 610483 for a quantum dot–based method to detect harmful bacteria in drinking water. The patent, titled 'Selective Capturing and Detection of Pathogens on Glass Matrix Using Affinity Moiety Coupled Quantum Dots', combines functionalised glass surfaces that capture bacteria with fluorescent quantum dots that emit a signal, allowing detection even when water appears normal. Demonstrated against Escherichia coli (E. coli), a gastrointestinal and waterborne pathogen, the technology promises portable, user-friendly water-testing kits for public health monitoring and drinking-water surveillance. Granted on 20 November 2026; application filed 14 February 2019. Led by Dr Gurpal Singh and Prof Bhupinder Singh Bhoop, with contributions from Taranvir Kaur, Anjali Pant, and Dr Ashish Suttee. The platform can be adapted to other pathogens by using specific recognition molecules.

article.articleHeadline: ICMR-NIV develops multiplex RT-PCR test to detect dengue, chikungunya, Zika simultaneously
article.articleSummary: ICMR-NIV, Pune, developed and validated a multiplex real-time RT-PCR test to detect dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses simultaneously from a single sample, enabling early differential diagnosis. Published in Archives of Virology on November 12, the assay was developed by NIV units in Pune, Alappuzha and Bengaluru, with AcSIR Ghaziabad; it targets dengue, chikungunya, and Zika with a human beta-actin internal control. In testing on 257 dengue-positive, 113 chikungunya-positive, 4 Zika-positive, and 220 negative samples, the assay showed clinical sensitivity of 95.3% for dengue (CI 91.99–97.56%), 98.2% for chikungunya (CI 93.64–99.78%), and 100% specificity for all three viruses. No cross-reactivity with related pathogens and correct classification of all samples in QCMD proficiency panels (2022–2025) were observed. The researchers note the need for more Zika-positive samples to validate performance; potential for commercial use and public health surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Hujan Lebat dan Genangan, Ahli Epidemiologi Unair Ingatkan Bahaya Leptospirosis
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Heavy Rain and Standing Water: UNAIR Epidemiologist Warns of the Danger of Leptospirosis
article.articleSummary: Heavy rain and standing water in Indonesia raise leptospirosis risk. Leptospira bacteria, shed in rat urine, contaminate floodwaters and can enter humans through feet or wounds. An epidemiologist from Universitas Airlangga notes transmission is more likely during monsoon/flood conditions when skin is exposed to contaminated water. Classic early symptoms are non-specific, including high fever, chills, yellowing of the eyes, and body pains, making early detection crucial. Diagnosis relies on serology and PCR to confirm Leptospira infection. Preventive measures during the wet season include wearing boots or protective footwear, protecting wounds, maintaining good hygiene (PHBS), vaccination, and keeping environments clean. BMKG weather alerts for the Riau Islands and West Sumatra on Nov 25, 2026 warn of heavy rain and potential floods. Anyone exposed to floodwater with fever or body pain should seek prompt medical care.

article.articleSummary: Influenza has entered the seasonal peak in China, per the National Disease Control Bureau. In China’s A-share market, influenza concept stocks surged with nearly 10 stocks hitting the daily limit-up, including Shuanglu Pharmaceutical, Kangzhi Pharmaceutical, and Hengdi Pharmaceutical as notable movers. Norovirus infection remains a focus for potential outbreaks in crowded venues, underscoring enteric disease risks in public settings. The remarks emphasize heightened vigilance for seasonal respiratory illness, imported vector-borne disease threats, and venue-based norovirus transmission, alongside market activity linked to influenza concept stocks in China.

article.articleHeadline: Bundibugyo Virus Disease Commonly Presents Without Haemorrhage in Outbreak
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus disease (BUDV) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) drives the largest outbreak on record, with 7,890 confirmed cases and 3,799 deaths across 63 health zones in seven provinces by late September 2026. Unlike classic Ebola hemorrhagic fever, BUDV often presents as a nonspecific febrile and gastroenteric illness; hemorrhagic signs occur in about 10.4% at presentation. Incubation ranges 2–21 days. In a dataset of 505 lab-confirmed cases (symptom details for 405), fever (74.3%), diarrhoea (67.4%), vomiting (66.7%), headache (42.2%), anorexia (39.5%), and abdominal pain (37.3%) predominate. Higher viral burden linked to mortality, with fatal cases showing lower PCR cycle-threshold values; average time from symptom onset to diagnostic sample collection was 7.4 days, highlighting diagnostic delays. Evidence gaps exist for children, pregnant women, and long-term sequelae. Clinical suspicion requires compatible symptoms plus epidemiological risk factors (active zones, contact with cases, exposure to blood, traditional burials, unprotected healthcare/lab duties).

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Flu season has begun; CDC experts: Even if you've had the flu, vaccination is still recommended.
article.articleSummary: China's influenza season has begun, with the National CDC warning that seasonal influenza and other acute respiratory infections are in the peak period. Dengue fever and chikungunya imported risk via mosquitos persists, while norovirus infections pose risks of outbreaks in crowded venues. At a November 24 briefing, experts explained common questions, including whether vaccination is needed after contracting influenza this year and misperceptions about vitamin C or self-treatment. China has rolled out multiple flu vaccination subsidies and services this year. Rural seniors (65+) and primary/secondary students will receive one free dose of the trivalent influenza vaccine, financed by government funds. Employee medical accounts can cover vaccine and injection service fees, and unions will fund vaccination for workers in new forms of employment. Weekend and special vaccination sessions are being promoted; the public is urged to book vaccinations promptly.

article.articleHeadline: Pigs Produce Broadly Reactive Influenza Antibodies Targeting Conserved
article.articleSummary: Porcine immune systems can generate monoclonal antibodies recognizing conserved influenza A structures and adaptive mutations across subtypes, per Pirbright Institute. Domestic swine co-circulate influenza A H1N1 and H3N2 with humans, and share lung anatomy and sialic acid receptor distribution, enhancing translational relevance. In the experiment, six five-week-old female Landrace-Hampshire cross pigs were intranasally infected with H3N2 A/Hong Kong/4801/2014 and, three weeks later, challenged intranasally with pandemic-line H1N1 A/Michigan/45/2015. Four days post-challenge, tracheobronchial lymph nodes were harvested; seven H3-specific porcine mAbs (H3-57 to H3-63; two kappa, five lambda) were cloned. H3-59, H3-60, and H3-62 neutralized H3 pseudoviruses bearing HK/5738/2014 HA; H3-57 bound egg-adapted HA with L194P (antigenic site B) and neutralized egg-adapted virus, but not wild-type. Mapping against eleven variants revealed epitope diversity. Overall, pigs generate antibody repertoires with translational relevance for tracking evolution, evaluating therapeutics, and guiding vaccine design against emerging pandemics.

article.articleHeadline: Gavi to procure 1.5 Mn doses of Ebola vaccine from Serum Institute to tackle Congo outbreak
article.articleSummary: Gavi will procure up to 1.5 million doses of ChAdOx1 BDBV, a candidate vaccine against Bundibugyo Ebola virus, from Serum Institute of India and Serum Life Sciences, financed through Gavi’s First Response Fund (FRF). Procurement depends on favorable trial outcomes, regulatory clearances, and deployment policy recommendations. ChAdOx1 BDBV, developed by the University of Oxford, is in a pivotal Phase 2/3 trial in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and is one of two Bundibugyo vaccine candidates WHO has recommended for evaluation during the ongoing outbreak. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo virus. The current outbreak has surpassed 11,000 cases across Africa, with DRC, Nigeria and Kenya among the hardest hit; the DRC has reported about 5,700 deaths. FRF, a rapid-response financing mechanism with $500 million, is part of Gavi’s Day Zero Facility. Gavi has committed up to $40 million for advance purchases with SII, plus $10 million for routine immunization, according to CEO Dr. Sania Nishtar.

article.articleHeadline: Trẻ mắc cúm A tăng, cha mẹ cần lưu ý gì?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rise in influenza A among children: what should parents pay attention to?
article.articleSummary: Influenza A in children rising at Cam Khe Regional Medical Center in Phu Tho Province, Vietnam, as of 25 November 2026, with pediatric admissions increasing. Influenza A is an acute respiratory infection caused by influenza A virus, transmitted mainly via respiratory droplets and contact with contaminated surfaces; schools and daycares are high-risk settings in enclosed, poorly ventilated spaces. Common signs include fever, chills, cough, sore throat, runny nose, headache, myalgias, and fatigue; in children nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, or diarrhea may occur. Seek medical care for suspected cases, especially if fever is persistent, seizures, breathing difficulties, fast breathing, chest pain, blue lips/limbs, lethargy, poor intake, or persistent vomiting. Prevention includes annual seasonal influenza vaccination, handwashing, masks in crowded places, covering coughs, and maintaining a clean, well-ventilated home. Complications can include bronchitis, pneumonia, otitis media, encephalitis, or exacerbation of underlying conditions. Early detection and treatment per physician guidance are crucial.

article.articleSummary: Gavi signs an advance purchase with Serum Institute of India to secure up to 1.5 million doses of the experimental Ebola vaccine ChAdOx1 BDBV, targeting Bundibugyo ebolavirus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo outbreak. Developed by University of Oxford with Serum Institute, vaccination will proceed only if safety and efficacy are demonstrated and regulatory approvals plus health authority recommendations are obtained, with coordination from the WHO. The outbreak in the DRC, ongoing since May 2026, has recorded more than 11,600 cases and over 5,700 deaths, most fatalities occurring in the Congo; there are currently no licensed vaccines or therapies specifically for Bundibugyo. Serum Institute has begun manufacturing components for over 500,000 doses to accelerate supply pending results and approvals. Gavi commits up to $40 million from its Initial Response Facility to facilitate access and scale production, plus $10 million for outbreak response and safeguarding routine vaccination and health workers. Sania Nishtar notes the need to complete regulatory pathways and distribution protocols with WHO.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue and other fever prevention measures: daily field survey of 100 houses to curb the breeding of aggressive mosquito larvae: Municipal Corporation Information - Dinakaran - Dinakaran
article.articleSummary: Dengue and other fever prevention measures are intensifying in Chennai as the northeast monsoon drives mosquito proliferation. The Chennai Metropolitan Corporation is conducting daily field surveys of about 100 houses per ward to eliminate breeding sites, remove items that collect water such as coconut husks, glass objects, and tires, and check water containers for larvae. Larvicides are applied to water-holding receptacles, and fogging is carried out in streets and homes. Given that Aedes aegypti mosquitoes—day-biting and breeding in stagnant water—propagate dengue, teams are inspecting wards 1–15 across schools, residences, streets, and rainwater drains to locate and remove breeding sites and carry out larviciding and fumigation. A total of 3,703 workers are involved, with each visiting 80–100 houses daily. Areas covered include Thiruvottiyur, Parth Nagar, Royapettah, Ambattur, Anna Nagar, and other localities across several wards (e.g., 121st, 144th, 168th, 172nd).

article.articleHeadline: 流感季出现新特点 这些防护要点请收好
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: New Features Emerge During Flu Season: Please Take Note of These Protective Measures.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-25, influenza activity in China has risen, with three co-circulating strains: A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B. Positive samples: 65.4% A(H1N1)/A(H3N2) and 34.6% B. The season is advancing earlier, with southern provinces rising from late September and northern provinces by late October. Co-circulation implies weak cross-protection; older adults, children, and those with chronic diseases face higher risk of repeated infections and severe illness. High-risk groups (65+, under 5, pregnant or perinatal, immune compromise, chronic diseases, obesity) should vaccinate promptly; vaccination remains the most effective prevention, and current uptake window is open. Antiviral drugs are prescription-only and target influenza, not the common cold, with potential side effects and resistance. After fever subsides, avoid strenuous activity for 1–3 weeks to reduce myocarditis risk; seek care for palpitations or chest pain.

article.articleHeadline: Kolom Pakar: Hewan dan Ancaman Pandemi Berikutnya
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Expert Column: Animals and the Next Pandemic Threat
article.articleSummary: Jakarta, Indonesia — BRIN hosted the CARE-I Grant Project (Collaborative Approach for Resilient Surveillance and Pandemic Preparedness in Indonesia) to strengthen animal pathogen genomic surveillance as pandemic preparedness, with capacity-building for researchers. On 24 November 2026, Prof Tjandra spoke at BRIN’s Ballroom Utama, Gatot Subroto, KST Sarwono Prawirohardjo, alongside BRIN Health Research Organization head Ni Luh Putu Indi Dharmayanti. He reviewed historical links between animals and pandemics, noting the 1918 influenza pandemic that infected about 500 million people and studies implicating birds, pigs, and horses. He cited papers associating pandemic risk with swine (H1N1 2009) and with COVID-19, discussing pangolins and bats as possible hosts and the Huanan Seafood Wholesale Market in Wuhan. He warned that future pandemics will likely involve animal transmission and may be waterborne or airborne, underscoring genomic surveillance as a foundation of preparedness.

article.articleHeadline: 마인드워크, AI 설계 에볼라 백신 후보 실험실 평가 착수
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mindwork begins laboratory evaluation of AI-designed Ebola vaccine candidate.
article.articleSummary: MindWalk Holdings Corp. reports completion of expression for the first Ebola vaccine design set and initiation of in vitro characterization, using HYFT technology and ReefIQ to target all human Ebola virus species. The computational design uses non-sequence HYFT pattern objects and ReefIQ's biological context layer to identify cross-species immunogens. The program aims to elicit immune responses against Zaire, Sudan, Bundibugyo, and Taï Forest ebolaviruses, not a single lineage. No universal Ebola vaccine exists; the approved product covers only Zaire ebolavirus. The Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo was declared a WHO PHEIC in May 2026, with over 11,000 cases and more than 5,500 deaths; cases have appeared in Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. The first immunogen set finished expression in Sept 2026; in vitro characterization is underway, with immunogenicity and serology tests to follow. Additional program updates are expected within a month.

triage.headline_ja: マインドワーク、AI設計エボラワクチン候補の実験室評価を開始
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス感染症は2026年5月にWHO PHEIC宣言済み。DRC、ウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリアでの流行状況（11,000例以上、5,500以上の死亡）が記載されており、IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。WPROスクリーニング基準も複数該当し、国際的な関心が高い。
triage.notes: 記事は新型ワクチン開発に関するニュースであるが、背景として既存のエボラウイルス流行（Bundibugyo系統）が詳述されている。DRCで確認されている流行が主題の対象国であり、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアは発生地域リストに含まれているが、記事本文では確定例の存在が述べられているのみ。対象国リストはDRC（203312）のみ該当。公開日時が2026年11月25日となっており、2026年5月のWHO PHEIC宣言後の継続流行として評価。

article.articleHeadline: RDC: la reprise des combats en Ituri fait craindre une nouvelle propagation d'Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: The resumption of fighting in Ituri raises fears of a new Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola has resumed in Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo, amid renewed fighting around Lopa, Lingi, Nizi and Inga Barrière, 25 km north of Bunia. The CRP halted its advance toward Bunia and pulled back from Inga Barrière, and remains engaged in Uganda-mediated peace talks; FARDC says it has routed the militiamen and controls Inga Barrière, Lopa and Lingi. Although a May ceasefire had held, clashes resumed, raising pressure ahead of negotiations. The outbreak in Ituri, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus; since May, 11,762 cases have been confirmed with 5,775 deaths. Population movements toward Bunia risk expanding transmission. On 24 November, WHO Chief Tedros evacuated health staff from Akwe hospital amid the fighting, highlighting threats to the response. No specific vaccine or treatment exists for Bundibugyo; two candidates will enter trials in Ituri, with Gavi agreeing to purchase up to 1.5 million doses, contingent on results and regulatory approval.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:イツリでの戦闘再燃でエボラ再拡大の懸念
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イツリ州で進行中の大規模エボラ流行（確定11,762例、死亡5,775例）が武力紛争の再燃により対応を阻害されており、住民移動による感染拡大リスクとWHO職員の避難など深刻な公衆衛生上の懸念がある。
triage.notes: Bundibugyoエボラウイルスによる流行で、既存ワクチン・治療法が存在しない点、武力紛争による対応中断とWHO職員の避難が特に懸念される。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: 男遊馬爾地夫染茲卡病毒　疾管署：返台「這期限內」避免或安全性行為
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Man who traveled to the Maldives contracted Zika virus; Taiwan CDC says, upon returning to Taiwan, during this period avoid sexual activity or practice safe sex.
article.articleSummary: Taiwan reports its second imported Zika virus infection this year in a northern Taiwan man in his 30s who traveled to the Maldives in early November. He developed fever and rash on November 13 after returning to Taiwan and was confirmed infected with Zika at Taoyuan International Airport; his travel companion contacts tested negative. As of November 23, Taiwan has two confirmed imported Zika cases (Thailand and Maldives); since 2016, 32 imported cases have been recorded, with 78.1% from Southeast Asia. Zika is primarily mosquito-borne but can spread sexually and vertically; about 20% of infections are symptomatic. Common symptoms include fever, rash, arthralgia, and conjunctivitis; infection during pregnancy may cause fetal microcephaly or death. Post-travel guidance includes at least 3 weeks of mosquito precautions and a 1-month blood donation deferral. Safe-sex recommendations: men 3 months and women 2 months after return; condoms or abstinence, especially if the partner is pregnant. Note: Bali travel advisory issued by CDC; broader regional context shows sustained, though lower, transmission.

triage.headline_ja: マルディブ旅行中にジカウイルスに感染した男性、疾病管理署が「台湾帰国後この期間は性交渉を控えるか安全な性行為を」と呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 台湾における輸入例の個別報告であり、重症度・異常性・国際的拡大のいずれも認められず、ルーティンの検疫対応として処理されている。
triage.notes: 本記事の主眼は台湾における輸入ジカ熱症例（感染地はモルディブ、対象国外）であるが、本年の既存輸入例としてタイ由来の症例、および広域的な注意喚起としてバリ島（インドネシア）への渡航勧告が言及されているため、対象国としてタイとインドネシアを記録した。モルディブは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Entenda como nasceu a Stratus, variante dominante da covid no Brasil
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Understand how Stratus originated, the dominant COVID variant in Brazil.
article.articleSummary: Stratus, an XFG descendant from Omicron, dominates Brazil’s 2026 COVID-19 landscape, accounting for about 90% of sequenced genomes (Diário do Grande ABC). Genomic surveillance analyzed 2,199 samples collected from week 1 through week 42 of 2026, with XFG/Stratus driving the majority of circulating viruses. The pattern coincides with regional upticks in severe COVID-19 cases in Mato Grosso (MT), Distrito Federal (DF), Rio de Janeiro (RJ), São Paulo (SP), and Santa Catarina (SC), though incidence remains low. The Ministry of Health and health authorities reinforce vaccination to prevent severe outcomes. Stratus originated from a recombination between LF.7 and LP.8.1.2, requiring simultaneous presence of both lineages in the same cell; the viral replication system can misalign, yielding a mosaic genome that became XFG/Stratus. The lineage is dominant in Brazil and advancing abroad, earning the Nimbus/Stratus naming trend.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジルで優勢な新型コロナ変異株「ストラタス」の成り立ちを理解する
triage.triage_reason: 既知のオミクロン系統（XFG/Stratus）の国内優勢化と重症例の地域的増加が報告されているが、全体として罹患率は低く、既存の対策（ワクチン接種推奨）で対応可能とされており、IHR基準の明確な該当は確認できない。
triage.notes: COVID-19変異株の系統学的解説記事であり、新規の公衆衛生緊急事態を示すものではない。重症例増加の地域（MT, DF, RJ, SP, SC）は報告されているが、全体的な罹患率は低いとされている。継続的なゲノムサーベイランスの動向を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: "تحالف عالمي" يعتزم توفير 1.5 مليون جرعة من لقاح تجريبي ضد "إيبولا"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "Global Alliance" plans to supply 1.5 million doses of an experimental Ebola vaccine.
article.articleSummary: As of 25 November 2026, the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunisation (GAVI) plans to purchase up to 1.5 million doses of an experimental Ebola vaccine targeting the Bundibugyo strain, pending proven safety and efficacy. The vaccine, developed by the University of Oxford and Serum Institute of India, is in clinical trials in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where no licensed vaccines or treatments exist for this strain, which has killed more than 5,700 people. GAVI has earmarked $40 million to support development and to accelerate distribution planning if results are favorable. GAVI’s Executive Director, Sania Nishtar, urged authorities to secure additional funding and expedite regulatory clearance and follow-up guidelines, hoping the World Health Organization will quickly issue guidance for use of the experimental vaccine.

triage.headline_ja: 「世界同盟（GAVI）」、エボラ治験ワクチンの150万回分供給を計画
triage.triage_reason: 記事はGAVIによる治験中エボラワクチン（Bundibugyo株対象）の調達計画に関する報道であり、新規発生や症例数・時期等の疫学情報が不足しているため、現時点でのRRA移行は見送り継続監視とする。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCで実施中のBundibugyo株エボラワクチン治験とGAVIによる調達・資金計画に関する内容で、新規発生イベントの詳細（症例数・期間・地域分布）は記載されていない。インドは開発元（Serum Institute of India）としての言及であり、発生地域には該当しない。英国もOxford大学の開発拠点として言及されているのみで除外。

article.articleHeadline: Peringatan Hujan Berlanjut, Ini 3M Plus Versi Kemenkes untuk Cegah DBD di Rumah
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Continued Rain Warning: Here’s the Ministry of Health’s 3M Plus Version to Prevent Dengue Fever at Home.
article.articleSummary: On 25 November 2026, BMKG issued morning rainfall alerts for East Java, Gorontalo, and Papua, warning standing water near homes fosters Aedes aegypti, the dengue vector. Indonesia’s Health Ministry notes dengue incidence tends to rise mid‑rainy season (January) with potential outbreaks, while mortality rates decline. The 3M Plus program prioritizes year‑round measures, especially during rains: drain and scrub water containers, seal storage, and reuse items likely to collect water. Plus measures include larvicidal powder, anti‑mosquito products, bed nets, larvivorous fish, and mosquito‑repellent plants, plus home lighting/ventilation tweaks and weekly vase‑water changes. The One House One Jumantik program designates a household larva monitor. Also cited are Wolbachia‑infected Aedes aegypti and a BPOM‑approved dengue vaccine, linked to 77.1% fewer infections and 82.6% fewer hospitalizations. Health facilities must report dengue signs within 3 hours and conduct epidemiologic investigations within 24 hours; Halo Kemenkes: 1500-567.

triage.triage_reason: 毎年の雨季に向けたデング熱予防の啓発・公衆衛生対策に関する定期的な注意喚起記事であり、異常な流行や急増を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 記事は季節的なデング熱予防啓発（3Mプラス、ワクチン、ウォルバキアなど）を内容としており、具体的な異常発生や感染拡大の報告はない。Papua New Guineaは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: WHO raises alarm over impact of conflict on Ebola containment efforts | Qatar Living
article.articleSummary: WHO warns that military operations in the Democratic Republic of Congo jeopardize Ebola containment, with Ebola response teams and staff trapped inside a hospital in Ituri province amid surrounding clashes. Evacuation has been impeded by ongoing fighting and heavy rains, and authorities hope to move personnel out as soon as possible. Hospitals in Ituri and North Kivu, the provinces most affected by the outbreak declared in mid-May, face persistent risks as the conflict continues around outbreak sites. Healthcare workers in the hospital’s maternity ward have taken refuge since fighting near the outbreak area began last Saturday. Ebola has historically claimed more than 15,000 lives in Africa over the past fifty years. The WHO emphasizes keeping hospitals as safe spaces and ensuring continued access for the ongoing response.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、コンゴ民主共和国の紛争がエボラ封じ込め活動に与える影響に警鐘
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の流行継続中にコンゴ民主共和国で武力紛争が発生し、対応チームが孤立するなど封じ込め活動に深刻な支障が出ており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: イトゥリ州・北キブ州で5月中旬に宣言されたエボラ流行が継続中。武力紛争により医療従事者・対応チームが病院内に孤立し、避難も困難な状況。WHOが病院の安全確保と対応継続の必要性を強調している。

article.articleHeadline: DBD di Jembrana Bali Turun Drastis, tetapi Musim Hujan Bawa Ancaman Baru, Ini Peringatan Dinkes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue Fever in Jembrana, Bali Drops Sharply, but Rainy Season Brings a New Threat, Health Office Warns
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever in Jembrana, Bali declined sharply through October 2026, with 19 cases, down from 119 infections in 2025 (no dengue-related deaths reported in 2025; 2026 fatalities not mentioned). Monthly counts for January–October 2026: 1, 2, 2, 2, 5, 2, 3, 0, 2, 0. The majority of cases appeared in Mendoyo District, with Puskesmas I Mendoyo reporting 5 cases to date. Health officials warn that the inter-monsoon and onset of the rainy season can heighten Aedes aegypti transmission and call for heightened vector-control measures. Recommended actions include home and community anti-mosquito campaigns (PSN) and eliminating standing water from bottles and plastic waste. The Jembrana Malaria Surveillance team is supporting efforts; residents are urged to burn plastic waste that can collect water to reduce breeding sites. Publication date: 2026-11-25.

triage.headline_ja: ジェンブラナ県（バリ）のデング熱は大幅減少、しかし雨季が新たな脅威をもたらす―保健局が警告
triage.triage_reason: デング熱症例数は前年から大幅減少しており、通常の季節的注意喚起の内容。異常性・深刻性・国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 症例数は119件（2025年）から19件（2026年10月時点）に減少。雨季到来に伴う媒介蚊対策の通常の注意喚起記事であり、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。

article.articleHeadline: Brasil -- Covid-19 volta a crescer no Brasil: entenda o avanço e os riscos da nova variante | Prensa Mercosur
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Brazil -- COVID-19 Is on the Rise Again in Brazil: Understand the Progression and Risks of the New Variant
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 is rising again in Brazil, with positivity up from 1% to 17% over three months, the highest since February, and Fiocruz reporting more SARI (severe acute respiratory infection) cases linked to the virus in some regions. By November 16, 2026, Brazil reported over 135,000 COVID-19–related ILI cases. Immunologist Ester Sabino notes waves typically occur twice yearly, now possibly triggered by a new lineage in a population with waning protection. The PJ.2.1 variant, detected in the second half of 2026, is more transmissible but not yet linked to greater severity; the WHO placed it on a monitoring list on November 19, with low global risk. Transmission persists via respiratory droplets, especially indoors with poor ventilation. Diagnostics rely on rapid antigen tests and RT-PCR; antiviral treatment via SUS is available for those 65+ and immunocompromised. Booster doses are advised for high-risk groups; routine vaccination includes children 6 months to 4 years.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジル -- 新型コロナウイルス感染症がブラジルで再び増加：新変異株の進行とリスクを解説
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19の季節性再流行であり、新変異株PJ.2.1はWHOにより監視対象とされたが世界的リスクは低いと評価されている。重症度上昇の明確な証拠はなく、国際的な異常事態とは言えないため経過観察に留める。
triage.notes: WHOはPJ.2.1変異株を2026年11月19日に監視リストに追加したが、世界的リスクは低いと評価。ブラジル国内の季節的な流行パターンの一部であり、重症度増加との明確な関連は報告されていない。

article.articleHeadline: منظمة الصحة العالمية تحذر من تأثير النزاع على جهود احتواء الإيبولا | قطر ليفنج
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization warns of the impact of the conflict on Ebola containment efforts | Qatar Living
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization warns that military operations in the Democratic Republic of Congo are undermining Ebola containment. WHO spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said several agency staff and Ebola response teams remain trapped inside a hospital in Ituri Province as heavy fighting continues nearby. He noted that the conflict, along with heavy rains, makes safe evacuation impossible, and stressed that hospitals must remain safe zones amid ongoing clashes in Ituri and North Kivu, the regions most affected by the outbreak. Hospital maternity staff have sought shelter in the facility since fighting began near the outbreak site weekend. The Ebola outbreak was declared in mid-May in the Democratic Republic of Congo; Ebola is a highly deadly virus that has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past five decades.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関、紛争がエボラ封じ込め努力に与える影響に警鐘 | Qatar Living
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行が進行中であり、武力紛争により封じ込め対応が妨げられているとWHOが警告している。公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクがあり、IHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: WHO職員やエボラ対応チームがイトゥリ州の病院内に閉じ込められている状況で、紛争と悪天候により安全な避難が不可能となっている。5月中旬に宣言されたエボラ流行が、紛争により封じ込めが困難になっているという深刻な状況。

article.articleHeadline: 3 Kondisi yang Bikin Bayi Rentan Alami Infeksi RSV yang Berat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Three Conditions That Predispose Infants to Severe RSV Infection.
article.articleSummary: RSV can infect anyone, but severe illness in infants is most likely among under six months, premature babies, and those with congenital heart disease. With narrow airways, infants—especially under six months—are prone to mucus buildup and airway inflammation from RSV. Prematurity means underdeveloped lungs; congenital heart disease worsens infection due to disrupted heart–lung circulation. Early RSV symptoms resemble a cold; danger signs include fast breathing: ≥60/min (<2 months), ≥50/min (2–12 months), ≥40/min (1–5 years), plus chest indrawing, lethargy, or poor feeding. RSV spreads via respiratory droplets and contaminated surfaces. Preventive options include maternal vaccination during pregnancy and monoclonal antibodies for high‑risk infants, though access in Indonesia is limited by cost and not in the national immunization program. Nonmedical home measures—handwashing, masks when someone is coughing, clean environments, and avoiding smoke—are crucial to curb transmission in Jakarta, Indonesia. Published November 25, 2026; Source: Liputan6.com, Jakarta.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue, Covid e Mpox deixam Rio Preto em alerta
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue, Covid, and Mpox Put Rio Preto on Alert.
article.articleSummary: Rio Preto, Brazil, warns about dengue, COVID-19, and mpox as threats. Dengue: 10,868 notifications this year, 5,648 confirmed cases, no deaths; Aedes aegypti infestation index 3.1% (vs 1% acceptable); larvae found in 310 of 10,000 inspected homes, with over 80% of breeding sites in backyards. Actions include educational blitzes, Saturday mutirões, and planned Wolbachia releases beginning January to reduce transmission. COVID-19: October positivity 2.4% (up from 1% Jun–Sept); potential rise in hospitalizations with lineage PJ.2.1 circulating in Brazil but not yet detected in Rio Preto. Mpox: nine cases this year; vaccines awaited from state health authorities. Vaccination status: dengue vaccine for 10–14-year-olds (two doses, 3 months apart); COVID-19 vaccines per PNI, with specific schedules for pregnant women, elderly, children 6 months–<5 years (Pfizer), and other groups. Stock: 1,650 dengue; 10,500 adult COVID; 3,800 pediatric COVID doses. Plans address El Niño impacts and arbovirus risks.

triage.triage_reason: 地域の公衆衛生当局による複数感染症の定例的な注意喚起であり、現時点で国際的拡大や重大な異常事態を示す根拠は乏しいが、デング熱の感染指数上昇やCOVID新系統の流行、mpox症例の継続など複数の経過観察点があるため監視を継続する。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus Tembus 140 Ribu, Rampeani Rachman Minta Malaria Center Buka 24 Jam
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cases surpass 140,000; Rampeani Rachman calls for the Malaria Center to open 24 hours.
article.articleSummary: Malaria cases exceed 140,000 in Mimika Regency, Central Papua, prompting calls to improve access to testing. Legislator Rampeani Rachman of the Perindo Party, in Commission III of the Mimika Regency DPRK, urged the Health Service to operate free malaria examinations at the Malaria Center 24 hours a day. While commending ongoing free screening programs, she cited limited service hours, treatment costs, and potential drug stockouts as barriers that could delay diagnosis and care. The proposal aims to ensure residents can be tested at any time, including night hours, with available medical staff. The appeal was made on Wednesday, 25 November 2026. The article notes the high burden of malaria in Mimika but does not provide details on laboratory confirmation or infection sources. No information on imported or exported cases was reported.

article.articleHeadline: منظمة الصحة العالمية تحذر من تداعيات القتال في الكونغو الديمقراطية على الاستجابة لتفشي " الإيبولا"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization warns of the repercussions of fighting in the Democratic Republic of the Congo on the response to the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: World Health Organization warns that armed operations in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are hampering the Ebola virus disease response. Ebola response staff remain trapped inside a hospital in Ituri Province as heavy combat around the facility and recent rains prevent safe evacuation; authorities hope evacuation can occur as soon as possible, ideally today. Healthcare workers in the hospital’s maternity ward have taken shelter since fighting began last Saturday near the area where the outbreak first emerged. Fighting continues in Ituri and North Kivu, the provinces hardest hit by the Ebola outbreak. In mid-May, the DRC announced an Ebola outbreak, a deadly disease that has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past five decades. WHO stresses that hospitals must remain safe spaces amid ongoing outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関（WHO）、コンゴ民主共和国における戦闘がエボラ出血熱流行への対応に及ぼす影響について警告
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目中3項目（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大リスク）に該当し、WPRO基準も全項目該当するためフルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: イトゥリ州での武力衝突によりエボラ対応スタッフが病院内に取り残され、対応活動が阻害されている状況。WHOが安全な医療空間の確保を強調しており、紛争地域での感染症対応の困難さが懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: 越南卫生部建议民众主动做好防护，应对新变异株
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Vietnam's Ministry of Health advises the public to actively take protective measures to cope with the new variant strain.
article.articleSummary: As of November 25, 2026, Vietnam’s Ministry of Health reports the SARS-CoV-2 variant PJ.2.1, following WHO’s November 19 preliminary risk assessment classifying PJ.2.1 as a monitored variant. While some countries report rising PJ.2.1 proportions in sequenced samples, there is no evidence this variant causes more severe disease or higher human-to-human transmission; WHO regards the global public health risk as low, with limited confidence. Vietnam’s Disease Prevention Bureau urges vigilance, not alarm. With winter–spring weather changes and year-end plus Lunar New Year gatherings, respiratory infections including COVID-19 may rise, especially in crowded, enclosed, poorly ventilated spaces. High-risk groups—older adults, those with underlying conditions, pregnant women, immunocompromised individuals, or on immunosuppressants—should proactively prevent infection and seek prompt care if symptoms appear. Protective measures: masking in healthcare settings, public transport, and crowded venues; hand hygiene; cough etiquette; ventilation. Seek care for fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, fatigue, or worsening symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: ベトナム保健省、新変異株に対応するため国民に自主的な防護措置を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: WHOはPJ.2.1変異株の世界的な公衆衛生リスクを低いと評価しており、重症化や感染力増加の証拠もない。ベトナム保健省の呼びかけは通常の季節的注意喚起であり、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: WHOはPJ.2.1をモニタリング対象変異株としているが、重症度・伝播性の増加の証拠はなく、リスクは低いとされている。記事は季節性呼吸器感染症への一般的な注意喚起であり、新たな公衆衛生上の脅威を示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: Smrtonosni virus se širi brže nego ikad: Ebola probila granice DR Konga i stigla do Evrope
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deadly virus spreading faster than ever: Ebola has breached the borders of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and reached Europe.
article.articleSummary: Largest Ebola outbreak in the DRC's history, with over 11,700 confirmed cases and 5,700 deaths as of 19 November; case fatality about 48.9%. The Bundibugjo strain drives rapid spread, with no licensed vaccines yet; three vaccine trials could yield a breakthrough by early 2027. The outbreak has crossed borders: Uganda 20 cases, 2 deaths; Kenya 9 cases, 2 deaths; Nigeria 1 case. Imported/exported infections: Germany 2 evacuees; Netherlands 1; France 1 (doctor returning from DR Congo); Switzerland 1 (infected; two evacuees); UK 1 (doctor evacuated, recovered). It began around February 2025; CDC estimates earlier start; WHO declared a public emergency mid-May; limited surveillance due to reduced humanitarian aid in 2025. Distrust of health workers fueled 260 attacks in six months. Measures: strengthen clinics and PPE, community outreach; border closures not effective. Vaccine development could change the course.

triage.headline_ja: 死をもたらすウイルスがかつてないスピードで拡大：エボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国の国境を越えヨーロッパに到達
triage.triage_reason: DRC史上最大規模のエボラ流行で11,700例超・致死率約49%、複数国への越境拡大とWHO公衆衛生緊急事態宣言により、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境拡大、及びドイツ・オランダ・フランス・スイス・英国への輸出例が報告されているが、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。ワクチン未承認（3件の治験中、2027年早期に結果期待）、人道支援減少による監視体制の弱体化、保健従事者への攻撃（6ヶ月で260件）など複合的リスクあり。

article.articleHeadline: UMS dan UNS pimpin Konsorsium 12 Perguruan Tinggi untuk percepatan eliminasi TBC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: UMS and UNS Lead the 12-University Consortium to Accelerate TB Elimination
article.articleSummary: Universitas Muhammadiyah Surakarta (UMS) is named Co-Academic Anchor in forming the 12-university TB Elimination Consortium led by Universitas Sebelas Maret (UNS) as Academic Anchor in Surakarta, Central Java. The consortium, officially launched on 24 November at UNS Tower, involves 12 higher education institutions, with participants including the Deputy Minister of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology Fauzan and Deputy Minister of Health Benjamin Paulus Octavianus, plus Central Java Governor Ahmad Luthfi and Surakarta Mayor Respati Ardi. UMS and UNS will coordinate with LLDIKTI Region VI to integrate academic, research, innovation and community service for TB control using a living laboratory approach. Four program stages: map, match, research, impact. Students across health, tech, data, and social sciences will contribute to education, digital solutions, behavior studies, and health communication. The effort targets accelerated TB elimination in Indonesia, emphasizing contact tracing, health education, and TB preventive therapy (TPT).

triage.headline_ja: UMSとUNSが結核撲滅加速化のための12大学コンソーシアムを主導
triage.triage_reason: 学術コンソーシアム設立という政策・研究協力に関する報道であり、新規発生や異常事態、公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す内容ではないため。
triage.notes: 既存の結核対策強化のための大学連携に関する発表記事であり、新規アウトブレイクの報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Brazilian Cashew Cheese Analogues Carry Low Pathogen Levels but Harbor
article.articleSummary: Brazilian 13 commercial cashew-based cheese analogue samples (Aug 2023–Jan 2024; retail markets, open fairs, and digital platforms) showed low conventional pathogen contamination: no Salmonella, coagulase-positive Staphylococcus, or Escherichia coli detected. However, opportunistic bacteria and antimicrobial-resistance concerns emerged. Bacillus cereus was confirmed in one sample by MALDI-TOF, while Cronobacter malonaticus and Delftia acidovorans appeared as atypical colonies on selective media, signaling potential public health relevance. Fungal analyses revealed elevated yeast and mold counts, with yeasts predominant, aligning with intended fermentation practices in products claiming probiotic, mesophilic, or vegan cultures; regulatory thresholds for molds/yeasts do not apply to matrices with viable cultures per Normative Instruction 313/2024. Fermentative flora included presumptive lactic acid bacteria in 10 of 13 samples, yielding 176 distinct isolates. The study followed ANVISA Norms (Annex I, 2022) and ISO-based microbiology protocols on 25-g portions to assess hygiene and regulatory compliance.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジル産カシューチーズ類似製品、病原体量は低いが耐性遺伝子を保有
triage.triage_reason: 食品微生物学的研究であり、実際の感染症発生やアウトブレイクの報告ではないため、公衆衛生上の緊急性やシグナルとしての該当性は認められない。
triage.notes: 本記事は特定の疾患アウトブレイクではなく、カシューチーズ代替品の微生物学的品質・規制適合性に関する研究報告である。主要病原体（サルモネラ、黄色ブドウ球菌、大腸菌）は検出されず、実際の感染症事例報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Training Yields Short-Term Gains and Persistent Gaps in Congo Study
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus–driven Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) prompted a focused training for non-healthcare Chinese nationals, as reported in Tropical Medicine and Health. By June 6, 2026, surveillance logged 515 confirmed cases and 91 deaths (case fatality rate 17.7%), across 25 health zones in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu, with 94% of cases in Ituri. In response, the 24th Chinese Medical Team delivered a five-session, in-person emergency-prevention curriculum in Chinese for expatriate workers. Using a single-group pre-post design, 200 attended; 190 completed both baseline and follow-up questionnaires (190 matched pairs). The curriculum covered viral characteristics, transmission, reporting, hand hygiene, and PPE donning/doffing with demonstrations. Post-training, significant short-term gains appeared across five domains, including higher median scores for psychological responses and scenario-based protective behavioral intentions, though gaps remained in incubation infectivity knowledge and PPE doffing contamination avoidance.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴにおけるエボラ研修調査：短期的な効果と残存する課題
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（515症例、91死亡、致死率17.7%）に関する情報を含み、IHR基準2つ以上（深刻な影響、異常性）に該当するためフルリスク評価へ進める。
triage.notes: 記事自体は中国人非医療従事者向けエボラ研修プログラムの評価研究だが、背景として2026年6月時点のDRCにおけるエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）アウトブレイク（イトゥリ州94%集中）の実データを含むため、アウトブレイクの継続状況を確認する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Hà Nội chủ động ngăn chặn nguy cơ dịch bệnh cuối năm
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hanoi Takes Proactive Measures to Prevent Year-End Epidemic Risk
article.articleSummary: Hanoi’s CDC, with Noi Bai International Airport, is bolstering surveillance for monkeypox among travelers from countries with ongoing transmission, with suspected cases sampled for confirmation at the National Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology and the National Hospital of Tropical Diseases. Hospitals are urged to ensure stocks, staffing, and funding to admit and treat cases and respond quickly to outbreaks. Monkeypox transmits via direct contact with lesions or body fluids, close respiratory exposure, shared items, sexual contact, mother-to-child transmission, and animal-to-human routes; symptoms include fever, headache, myalgia, lymphadenopathy, malaise, and vesiculopustular rash. Most recover in weeks, but young children, pregnant women, and the immunocompromised are higher risk; guidance stresses avoiding panic and seeking medical advice for suspected cases. In dengue, Hanoi reported 506 cases (13–20 Nov, 92 wards) and 7,532 year-to-date (122 wards), with 285 outbreaks and 19 active. Hand, foot, mouth disease: 66 cases; pertussis: 133; tetanus: 18 with 1 death. Ho Chi Minh City: 2,428 dengue (9–15 Nov; 49,232 year-to-date). Nationwide dengue >170,000 in 10 months with 21 deaths; four dengue serotypes circulating. Authorities maintain surveillance, vector control, and autumn–winter readiness in schools and crowded settings.

triage.headline_ja: ハノイ、年末の感染症リスクに対する予防的対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: ハノイ・ホーチミン市における季節性デング熱の流行継続とサル痘（Mpox）監視体制の強化を報じるルーチン的な公衆衛生対策記事であり、新規の異常なアウトブレイクは確認されていないが、複数疾患の動向を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 記事は主にハノイ・ホーチミン市における季節性デング熱流行の継続報告と、Mpoxに対する空港・病院での監視体制強化についてのルーチン的な公衆衛生対策記事。百日咳・破傷風も言及されているが新規の異常事態の報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: New Ebola Vaccines Enter Trials As WHO Temporarily Relocates Teams Due To Insecurity In Congo
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-25, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s eastern and northeastern regions remains the worst outbreak on record, with 11,762 confirmed cases and 5,775 deaths, centered in Ituri province. Insecurity has forced the temporary relocation of WHO and partner teams; staff sheltered for three days at a hospital in Akwe, Ituri, before evacuation under challenging conditions. The outbreak is driven by the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccines or treatments exist yet. Two Bundibugyo-specific vaccines are entering clinical trials in Ituri: ChAdOx1 (adenoviral vector) developed by the University of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India, and mRNA-1469 from Moderna. Gavi has signed an advance purchase commitment with SII and Serum Life Sciences to secure up to 1.5 million doses of ChAdOx1, contingent on trial success and regulatory approval. Escalating attacks since late October continue to hamper Ebola response efforts in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴにおける治安悪化によりWHOチームが一時避難、新型エボラワクチンの治験が開始
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラ流行(感染者11,762人、死者5,775人)が継続しており、治安悪化によりWHO対応チームが退避するなど深刻な公衆衛生上の懸念と国際支援の必要性が明確であるため。
triage.notes: インドと英国はワクチン開発企業(オックスフォード大学、インド血清研究所、Moderna)の所在地として言及されているのみで、実際の発生地域ではないためverified_locationsから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Dinkesda Blora Catat Kasus HIV di Blora Capai 1.354 Orang hingga Oktober 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Blora Regency Health Office records HIV cases in Blora, reaching 1,354 people as of October 2026.
article.articleSummary: Blora Regency's Health Office (Dinkesda) reports 1,354 people living with HIV (ODHIV) in Blora as of October 2026, about 88% of the 2026 target of 1,536 cases. Of these, 758 are on antiretroviral therapy (ARV). From January to October 2026, 158 new HIV cases were identified, with 129 initiating treatment. HIV remains incurable, but ARV regimens suppress viral replication and maintain immunity when taken regularly, enabling longer, healthier lives. The program emphasizes preventing transmission to uninfected individuals and ensuring ongoing treatment for those infected; adherence is crucial, with reports of patients on ARV for 15–20 years who remain controlled.

triage.headline_ja: ブローラ県保健局、2026年10月までのHIV感染者数1,354人と発表
triage.triage_reason: 既知の慢性感染症であるHIVの地域統計報告であり、突発的な公衆衛生上の異常事象ではないため、通常のサーベイランス範囲内と判断する。
triage.notes: 累計感染者数の定期報告であり、新規の異常増加や公衆衛生危機を示す内容ではない。

article.articleHeadline: 43 fall ill after eating chicken shawarma in Maharashtra's Bhiwandi - english.punjabkesari.com
article.articleSummary: Suspected food poisoning from chicken shawarma sold at a roadside stall near Vanjar Patti Naka, Bhiwandi, Maharashtra, sickened 43 people (including 10 children) aged 2–40 years; a pregnant woman is among those admitted. Symptoms include vomiting, diarrhoea, and fever. Affected individuals have been hospitalized at the Indira Gandhi Memorial (IGM) Sub-District Hospital in Bhiwandi. Officials warn of a potential cluster linked to the same stall, with multiple patrons falling ill within a short period after eating the shawarma. Some patients reported illness began the day after consumption and remained persistent. No laboratory confirmation details are provided in the report. Information sourced from IANS, published on 25 November 2026.

triage.headline_ja: マハラシュトラ州ビワンディでチキンシャワルマを食べた43人が体調不良
triage.triage_reason: 単一の屋台に関連した食中毒の疑いで、国際的拡大や公衆衛生上の深刻な脅威を示す要素がなく、散発的な食品安全事例と考えられる。
triage.notes: 食中毒（疑い）事例であり感染症のアウトブレイクではない可能性が高い。検査確認情報なし。

article.articleHeadline: Congo-Kinshasa: The DR Congo's Ebola Crisis Revives an Old Ethical Question - What Do Health Workers Owe Patients?
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak declared by the World Health Organization on May 15, 2026 in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). By November 18, 2026, there were 11,712 cases and 5,720 deaths, nearly all in the DRC. No approved vaccines or therapeutics yet; early detection and supportive care essential, requiring intense coordination among clinicians, nurses, sanitation staff, public health workers, volunteers and community health workers. As of August 2026, 160 health workers contracted Ebola and 43 died. This situation prompts a core bioethics question: what do health workers owe patients, and is protection of workers a prerequisite for outbreak control? Historical ethics (1847 AMA code) mandate duty to treat; debates consider risk, consent, training, social contract, and vaccine access. The crisis is compounded by violence against health workers in eastern DRC: 81 attacks May 2026–Nov 18, 2026, causing 5 deaths and 34 injuries (29 facility attacks). August 2026 reports indicate over 260 attacks and eight health workers killed. Community fear and disruption of burial rites further hinder response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国:DRCのエボラ危機が古い倫理的問題を再燃させる - 医療従事者は患者に何を負っているのか？
triage.triage_reason: DRCで大規模なエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（11,712症例、5,720死亡）が継続しており、医療従事者への暴力や治療法未承認など公衆衛生上深刻な影響を伴う重大シグナルである。
triage.notes: 発生地域に記載されたUgandaおよびBundibugyoは、エボラウイルスの系統名（Bundibugyo ebolavirus）に由来する混同と考えられ、記事本文はDRC国内のアウトブレイクのみを扱っているためUgandaは除外した。既にWHOが宣言した既知の大規模アウトブレイクであり、ワクチン・治療薬未承認、医療従事者への暴力など深刻な状況が継続している。

article.articleHeadline: 三种流感毒株叠加来袭，流感概念股掀起涨停潮
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Three influenza virus strains converge, sparking a wave of limit-ups in influenza-related stocks.
article.articleSummary: Influenza season in China has entered the epidemic period with three strains circulating: Influenza A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and Influenza B/Victoria. National surveillance through 2026-11-15 shows H1N1 56.2%, H3N2 15.5%, and B/Victoria 28.3% of positives. Tianjin upgraded its influenza alert to Level III this week, reporting predominance of A(H1N1) in the city, followed by B/Victoria and A(H3N2). Vaccination guidance stresses early protection: antibodies typically develop 2–4 weeks after vaccination; early vaccination is encouraged, though vaccination can occur any time during the season. This year, vaccine supply shifts toward predominantly trivalent vaccines. Policy supports free vaccination for rural residents aged 65+ and for primary/secondary school students, with financial mechanisms via payroll accounts and unions to expand coverage. Antivirals include oseltamivir, baloxavir marboxil, favipiravir, and zanamivir; overall supply is adequate, though short-term regional shortages may occur. The oseltamivir producer notes full end-to-end production capacity to ensure nationwide access.

triage.headline_ja: 三種のインフルエンザウイルス株が重なって流行、インフルエンザ関連株が値幅制限上限（ストップ高）の波を巻き起こす
triage.triage_reason: 中国における季節性インフルエンザの通常のサーベイランス報告であり、A(H1N1)・A(H3N2)・B(Victoria)の同時流行は例年見られるパターン。重症化や死亡の急増、異常な拡大の兆候はなく、記事の主眼も株式市場の反応に関するものである。
triage.notes: 記事は天津での警戒レベル引き上げと全国的なインフルエンザサーベイランスデータ、ワクチン・抗ウイルス薬供給状況を報告する季節性の定例的な内容であり、特段の異常事態は認められない。株式市場への影響に焦点を当てた経済ニュースとしての側面が強い。

article.articleHeadline: عائد من الكونغو يخضع للعزل والفحوصات للاشتباه بإصابته بالإيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A returnee from the Congo is placed in isolation and undergoes testing for suspected Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Suspected Ebola case in Israel after a return from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The Health Ministry received a report of Ebola-like symptoms and treats this as a suspected case; laboratory tests and investigations are underway. The patient has been moved to Ichilov Medical Center in Tel Aviv and is in isolation under high-containment protocols. An epidemiological investigation is identifying contacts; those not reached are not currently required to act. Ebola is transmitted by direct contact with an ill person or their blood and body fluids, contaminated objects, or infected animals. A series of tests will confirm the suspicion. Israel is monitoring the Congo outbreak, has strengthened hospital readiness, and has mechanisms to detect potential cases among travelers from affected areas. Travelers returning from Congo with fever over 38°C or unusual symptoms within 21 days should stay home and call 5400; avoid visiting clinics without prior coordination. No confirmed Ebola cases in Israel yet.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ帰国者がエボラ感染疑いで隔離・検査を受ける
triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ流行地からの帰国者がイスラエルで疑い症例として隔離・検査中であり、確定すれば国際的拡散・渡航制限等のリスクを伴うためフルRRAでの確認が望ましい。
triage.notes: 本記事の主題はイスラエル（対象国外）における帰国者のエボラ疑い症例であり、DRCでの発生自体を報じるものではないため、DRCは背景情報として扱い verified_locations には含めていない。確定診断は未了（No confirmed Ebola cases in Israel yet）。

article.articleHeadline: 茲卡今年第2例境外移入 返國後4件事別忘
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Zika: This year's second imported case; four things to remember after returning to the country.
article.articleSummary: Taiwan reports the year’s second imported Zika virus infection: a man in his 30s from northern Taiwan, who travelled to the Maldives in early November and returned November 13 with fever and rash; infection confirmed at Taoyuan Airport quarantine. The cohabitant is asymptomatic and test-negative. Zika is a Flavivirus mainly transmitted by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, with possible sexual, vertical, or transfusion transmission. Incubation 3–14 days; about 80% are asymptomatic; typical symptoms include fever, rash, arthralgia, and conjunctivitis; no vaccine is available. As of November 23, Taiwan has two imported Zika cases (Thailand and Maldives). Since 2016, 32 imported cases overall, with 78.1% from Southeast Asia (Thailand 8, Vietnam 6). WHO data through May 2026 show 97 countries/regions with local mosquito-borne transmission. Bali and Maldives travellers have returned with cases; US CDC has a Level 2 alert for Bali. Post-return guidance emphasizes: safe sex, mosquito prevention, delaying blood donation, and monitoring symptoms for two weeks; seek care if fever/rash/arthralgia/conjunctivitis, and avoid NSAIDs during fever; call 1922 or 0800-001922.

triage.headline_ja: 茲卡熱、今年第2例の海外感染症例 ― 帰国後に注意すべき4つのこと
triage.triage_reason: 台湾における輸入性ジカウイルス感染症の単発事例であり、現地での二次感染や流行の兆候はなく、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 感染地はモルディブへの渡航歴によるものであり、台湾は検疫で発見した場所に過ぎない。モルディブ・台湾ともに対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空。タイ・ベトナム・インドネシア・バリは過去の統計上の言及に過ぎず、本イベントの発生地ではない。
