article.articleSummary: Kaohsiung’s Gushan District dengue outbreak expands with 3 new local cases announced on Nov 25, raising the district’s cluster to seven and Kaohsiung’s local total to 22 this year. The cases (ages 51–56; onset Nov 22–23) include an employee at Xiaobei Department Store Qingfeng branch; authorities found Aedes breeding sources in the store’s water troughs and canvas containers, designating the venue as high-risk. People who visited since Nov 1 are urged to test; 534 tested so far with one positive (case 17). The other two cases are cohabitants in Yuxingli, part of the same community transmission. Another case with onset Nov 18 tested positive for dengue virus type 2; source under investigation. Nationwide total: 267 confirmed; 27 local (22 in Kaohsiung); 240 imported (Vietnam 73, Philippines 38, Indonesia 32). Testing incentives include 100 NT voucher; Cosmed on Qingfeng Street. Seek care for fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, rash and report travel history.

article.articleHeadline: Reported dengue cases worldwide rose 34-fold -- Nature
article.articleSummary: Dengue cases worldwide rose 34-fold from 430,000 in 1990 to 14.7 million in 2024, per a new analysis presented November 22 at the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene meeting in National Harbor, Maryland (Nature reports). Dengue is a viral disease transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in warm urban environments, with symptoms including fever, headaches and severe bone pain. Researchers combined diverse databases and used statistical modelling to fill gaps in historical data. The finding underscores a global surge linked to urbanization. In Brazil, the first randomized Wolbachia trial in the Americas assessed dengue transmission; 32 million Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes were released from January 2021 to May 2022 in designated areas, with nearly 6,000 children monitored and annual blood samples from 2020–2024. Children in Wolbachia areas had a 68% lower likelihood of dengue infection than those outside.

article.articleHeadline: 基础性疾病患者需重点防范流感_ 沈报早读_新闻中心_沈阳网
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Patients with underlying conditions should take extra precautions to prevent influenza.
article.articleSummary: National influenza activity is at a mid-season level, with influenza A, especially H1N1, predominant nationwide; Shenyang's latest surveillance shows H1N1 is overwhelmingly prevalent there. A/H1N1 influenza typically causes higher fever, cough, sore throat, headache, myalgia, and fatigue; some patients may have vomiting or diarrhea. People with chronic diseases—hypertension, coronary heart disease, diabetes, chronic respiratory disease—along with children, the elderly, and pregnant women, face higher risk of complications such as pneumonia, respiratory failure, or heart failure, and possible worsening of underlying conditions. Precautions include timely influenza vaccination (protective antibodies need 2–4 weeks; vaccination can be given during Oct–Mar; earlier is better). Maintain chronic disease management, monitor blood pressure, glucose, oxygen, and lung function; avoid stopping meds. Seek medical care within 48 hours of symptom onset to evaluate antivirals; beware warning signs. Practice masking, hygiene, ventilation, and separation for ill household members.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How a Particular Species of Mosquito Is Being Used in Dengue Prevention
article.articleSummary: Dengue and other mosquito-borne diseases are being tackled in Brazil using Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti instead of conventional insecticides. In Belo Horizonte, the EVITA long-term trial involving over 5,700 schoolchildren showed dengue and chikungunya infections fell by about 68-69% in areas released with Wolbachia mosquitoes compared with control areas. The technique works by introducing Wolbachia—a safe bacterium not normally in Ae. aegypti—into mosquitoes, which blocks replication of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses, so a bite does not transmit them. The release does not kill mosquitoes; instead, infected mosquitoes are released to mate with wild ones, spreading the trait across generations. The World Mosquito Program has recognized it as a safe and eco-friendly dengue control method, and Brazil has launched the world's largest production center to generate about 100 million Wolbachia-carrying mosquito eggs weekly. Releases include adult mosquitoes or eggs in take-away boxes, aiming for long-term establishment.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Liaoning Issues Tiered Influenza Alert
article.articleSummary: As of November 25, 2026, Liaoning issues Tiered Influenza Alert; current province-wide activity is Level III, indicating moderate spread. Influenza-like illness (ILI) accounts for 5.59% of emergency and outpatient visits, above the baseline 4.11%. Circulating strains are predominantly A/H1N1, with concurrent activity of A/H3N2 and B/Victoria lineage. Multi-pathogen surveillance shows the top pathogens in influenza-like illness are influenza virus, rhinovirus, and enterovirus. Activity is expected to rise this week. Officials urge vaccination, with free flu vaccine offered to rural-area residents aged 65+ and to elementary/middle school students. Recommendations include resting at home for flu-like symptoms, wearing masks in public or indoor settings, seeking medical care if needed, and precise management for chronic respiratory patients. Additional measures include monitoring absenteeism in schools/daycares, maintaining hygiene and ventilation, and obtaining prevention information from official Liaoning CDC channels. Report by Shenyang Daily Media.

article.articleHeadline: Les combats en République démocratique du Congo perturbent la lutte contre l'Ebola | L'actualité
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fighting in the Democratic Republic of the Congo disrupts the fight against Ebola | L'actualité
article.articleSummary: Fighting in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo disrupts the Ebola response. Since May, the outbreak has infected over 11,700 people and caused more than 5,700 deaths, making it the country’s deadliest of 17 outbreaks and likely to surpass West Africa’s 2014–2016 toll of about 11,000. Ebola spreads through direct contact with blood or other bodily fluids of the sick or deceased; containment relies on rapid isolation, contact tracing, and safe burial. Intense clashes between government forces and rebels near Bunia, Ituri province, have blocked access to communities, hindered contact tracing, and reduced staff at treatment centers. The WHO evacuated around ten people, including two staff and Congolese health officials, after they were trapped in Akwe; operations were moved from Mongbwalu to Bunia. In Nord-Kivu, attacks displaced over 20,000, further complicating tracing. Some local teams resumed work on Wednesday; WHO operations continue in Bunia.

article.articleHeadline: Clinical Scoring Tool Distinguishes Lethal Viral Infection From Scrub
article.articleSummary: Jeju National University Hospital, South Korea, evaluated the Tick-borne Infection Severity Score (TISS), an eschar-independent six-variable tool to distinguish severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) from scrub typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi) in East Asia. Retrospective analysis included 101 RT-PCR–confirmed SFTS cases (2013–2024) and 194 scrub typhus cases (2003–2012; 2022–2024). Among 241 cases with complete data, the score achieved an AUROC of 0.985 (95% CI 0.973–0.997). At a five-point threshold, sensitivity was 99.0% and specificity 84.4% (119/141 scrub typhus correctly identified); at eight points, specificity was 97.2% and sensitivity 90.0% (90/100 SFTS in the highest tier; 4 scrub typhus). Score components: absence of rash (2), altered mental status (2), platelets <100,000/µL (2), WBC <4,000/µL (3), CRP ≤3 mg/dL (3), lymphocytes >30% (1). SFTS shows bone marrow suppression with leukopenia/thrombocytopenia; scrub typhus involves endothelial inflammation with high CRP. Mortality is higher for SFTS than scrub typhus.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The United States experiences its worst measles outbreak in decades, claiming nine lives; a quick overview of global public health and medical highlights.

In the UK, summer 2026 heat deaths reached 5,258—the highest since 2016. WHO notes a Yakima County, Washington avian influenza outbreak with 3 adult cases and 1 death. In pharmaceuticals, Roche’s Wilserdly for early-stage breast cancer wins FDA approval, the first similar hormone therapy in over two decades; GSK’s next-gen asthma drug shows promise, potentially reducing dosing frequency for rare immune diseases.

article.articleHeadline: Health Workers in Southern Brazil Report Gaps in Municipal Leptospirosis
article.articleSummary: Leptospirosis remains a major public health challenge in Southern Brazil, particularly in flood-prone and border territories. A qualitative study of healthcare workers in a Southern Brazilian municipality, published in BMC Public Health, identifies substantial gaps in municipal prevention and control, with professionals calling for integration of leptospirosis into routine primary care and health surveillance, and highlighting limitations in state-level planning. Using Etnograph for data management and thematic content analysis across pre-analysis, material exploration, and results treatment, the study develops four analytical categories capturing perspectives on prevention, diagnosis, and control. Authors conclude that frontline viewpoints illuminate critical deficiencies in current responses and suggest directions to strengthen prevention and control; they advocate further in-depth exploration of previously unexplored topics. Published 2026-11-25.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: D-Day Against Dengue: Leopoldina City Hall promotes a large cleanup drive, vaccination and leisure activities in the São Cristóvão neighborhood.
article.articleSummary: Leopoldina’s São Cristóvão neighborhood hosts D-Day Against Dengue: Minas Unida no Combate ao Aedes on Saturday, November 28, 2026, from 8:00 to 12:00, organized by the City Hall’s Endemias sector. The event combines prevention, sanitation, and community activities to curb Aedes breeding. A cleaning drive will see endemic agents conduct home visits, with the Bota-Fora truck collecting electronic waste, glass, recyclables, tires, and used oil. Residents delivering five plastic containers that can collect water can swap them for popsicles or plant seedlings in a sustainable exchange. The Vacimóvel will update vaccination records. The program includes capoeira, bouncy castle, cotton candy, popcorn, and children's recreation. The aim is to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and strengthen protection against dengue through cleaning and vaccination outreach in São Cristóvão.

article.articleSummary: On Saturday, November 28, 2026, Joinville participates in the National Day of Mobilization against dengue, Zika, and chikungunya, with educational activities in the Bucarein (Fort Atacadista) and Boa Vista (Cooper Atacarejo) neighborhoods and indoor residual spraying at Arena Joinville, providing 60–90 days of protection by killing contact with treated surfaces. On Friday, November 27, environmental surveillance, civil defense, municipal guards, community health agents and the 62nd Infantry Battalion will conduct awareness in the Norte Industrial Zone, visiting homes and businesses to inspect breeding sites and apply preventive treatment as needed. The arena spray forms a protective film lasting 60–90 days; this year the approach was used in 169 public spaces and 182 risk sites, including junkyards and recycling facilities, with fludora perifocal. Prevention centers on eliminating standing water; hotspots can be reported via the Joinville Fácil app or city ombudsman.

article.articleHeadline: ES recebe 80 mil testes rápidos e mobiliza municípios para lidar com Covid-19 - Folha Vitória
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Espírito Santo receives 80,000 rapid tests and mobilizes municipalities to tackle COVID-19 - Folha Vitória
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 activity rises in Espírito Santo, Brazil, with 4,600+ cases of COVID-19-related influenza-like illness and 17 deaths in 2026 reported by Nov 21. On Nov 24, the State Health Secretariat (Sesa) and the Espírito Santo Municipal Health Secretaries Council (Cosems/ES) held an online meeting with over 100 connected devices to discuss vaccination, testing, and care. Subsecretary Orlei Cardoso highlighted that among the deceased, 14 were unvaccinated and 3 had incomplete schedules, and urged expanding vaccination to priority groups: children, the elderly, and pregnant women. The state received 80,000 rapid tests for COVID-19, with distribution to regional health units; another 200,000 are expected next week. Tests do not replace RT-PCR; samples go to Lacen/ES for confirmation and sequencing. The note advocates leveraging testing to boost vaccination, and reinforces precautions: hand hygiene, masking with symptoms, ventilation, isolation for five days from the test date, and up-to-date vaccination for COVID-19, influenza, and RSV.

triage.headline_ja: エスピリト・サント州が8万個の迅速検査キットを受領、新型コロナウイルス対策のため市町村を動員
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル国内の一地方州における季節性のCOVID-19対応（検査キット配布・ワクチン接種呼びかけ）に関する通常の行政広報であり、IHR基準・国際的拡大リスクともに該当せず、社会的関心も地方レベルにとどまる。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジル・エスピリト・サント州における季節性COVID-19対応の行政広報であり、州保健局が検査キット配布とワクチン接種拡大を呼びかける内容。国際的な公衆衛生上の懸念材料は確認されない。

article.articleHeadline: ஒசூரில் டெங்கு கொசு ஒழிப்புப் பணி தீவிரம்
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue mosquito eradication operations intensified in Osur
article.articleSummary: As of 25 November 2026, Osur municipality is intensifying dengue and other mosquito-borne disease prevention across all 45 wards. Public-health teams are conducting expanded vector-control activities, including insecticide spraying (fogging) in residential areas, streets, and roadside spots with high mosquito production. Efforts also target open water-collection areas, stagnant drains, and containers to curb Aedes mosquito breeding. To protect public health and limit dengue transmission, measures to suppress the Aedes population are being implemented. Residents are urged to prevent water stagnation around homes, keep water-storage vessels tightly closed, and clean water containers weekly. The municipality calls for public cooperation to help create a dengue-free Osur.

triage.headline_ja: ホスールでデング熱媒介蚊の駆除活動が強化
triage.triage_reason: インドの一都市における定例的なデング熱媒介蚊対策活動の報道であり、異常な流行拡大や重症化の情報はなく、通常の公衆衛生活動の範囲内と判断される。
triage.notes: 記事は地方自治体による予防的な蚊駆除活動（フォギング、水溜まり対策等）を報じるもので、具体的な症例数や死亡者数、流行拡大の情報は含まれていない。

article.articleHeadline: Immunocompromised Adults Face Higher Risk of Severe Dengue
article.articleSummary: Thailand-based multicenter retrospective cohort study of 894 laboratory-confirmed dengue patients (Jan 2023–Jun 2024) found immunocompromised adults (n=59) have markedly higher risk of severe dengue per WHO 2009 criteria: 22% vs 4.9% in non-immunocompromised. Immunocompromised patients were older (median 47.0 vs 33.5 years) and had a higher Charlson comorbidity index (median 1 vs 0). Fever was absent more often among immunocompromised (10.2% vs 1.1%). Platelet nadirs were lower with prolonged thrombocytopenia. Higher hospital admission rates, longer length of stay, and increased 30-day mortality were observed. After adjustment, immunocompromised status associated with severe dengue (OR 3.43) and higher comorbidity index (OR 1.33). Authors urge improved prevention and clinical management strategies for this vulnerable population. Published in PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: 免疫不全成人はデング重症化リスクが高い
triage.triage_reason: 既存疾患であるデング熱に関する学術研究報告であり、新規の公衆衛生イベントや異常な発生を示すものではないため。
triage.notes: 本記事はタイにおけるコホート研究の学術論文（PLOS NTDs掲載）であり、新規アウトブレイクの報告ではない。SFTSウイルスへの言及はサマリー中になく、疾患名リストへの混在は誤タグの可能性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Paciente com suspeita de Mpox que fugiu de hospital é localizado e internado novamente em MG
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Patient with suspected Mpox who escaped from hospital is located and readmitted in Minas Gerais.
article.articleSummary: 36-year-old man with suspected Mpox escaped from Hospital Universitário in Divinópolis, Minas Gerais, Brazil, and was located in the Niterói neighborhood and readmitted to the facility. Mpox is a contagious, notifiable disease that requires isolation; breach of sanitary measures can lead to detention and fines. Initially, municipal health officials said he had been diagnosed, but a later update stated he presents clinical features compatible with Mpox and is awaiting laboratory confirmation. He remains hospitalized under medical supervision, with no disclosed motive for the escape. Mpox transmission occurs mainly through direct contact with skin lesions, secretions, and contaminated objects. The health department emphasizes that non-compliance with isolation can be considered a crime under Brazilian law (Article 268 of the Penal Code), with penalties of detention for one month to one year plus fines, and other sanctions may apply depending on circumstances.

triage.headline_ja: 病院から逃走したMpox疑い患者が発見され、ミナスジェライス州で再入院
triage.triage_reason: 単一の疑い症例（検査確定前）であり、個人の隔離違反に関する地方ニュース。公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や国際的拡大のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 検査確定前の単一疑い症例に関する地方ニュース記事。患者の逃走・隔離違反に関する法的側面が主題であり、公衆衛生上の重大性は限定的。

article.articleHeadline: Covid-19: o único estado em alerta para casos graves
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19: the only state on alert for severe cases.
article.articleSummary: Rio de Janeiro state has reached an alert level for COVID-19 incidence, driven by concurrent circulation of multiple pathogens. A Health Ministry bulletin attributes the rise in severe acute respiratory syndrome cases in Rio to the simultaneous activity of SARS-CoV-2, human metapneumovirus, and influenza A and B viruses, with long-term growth markers rising over the past six weeks up to epidemiological week 45. Nationwide, Brazil remains at low risk for severe COVID-19, but signals of higher transmission have been detected in the Distrito Federal (Brasília) and 21 states, prompting ongoing surveillance. As of November 16, Brazil recorded 135,378 influenza-like illness diagnoses attributed to COVID-19, underscoring persistent viral circulation across regions. The data emphasize continued monitoring of COVID-19 alongside other respiratory pathogens and the potential for co-infections, even as overall risk stays low outside Rio.

triage.headline_ja: COVID-19：重症化アラートが出ている唯一の州
triage.triage_reason: リオデジャネイロ州でCOVID-19重症例の警戒レベルに達し複数病原体の同時流行が確認されているが、ブラジル全体では低リスクとされており、国際的拡大や渡航制限等の懸念は明確でないため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: リオデジャネイロ州でCOVID-19、ヒトメタニューモウイルス、インフルエンザA/Bの同時流行による重症急性呼吸器症候群の増加が報告されているが、ブラジル全国としては低リスクと評価されている。保健省の国内モニタリング事案であり、国際的な懸念は現時点で確認されない。

article.articleHeadline: Paciente com Mpox que havia abandonado hospital é encontrado em Divinópolis
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mpox patient who had left the hospital is found in Divinópolis.
article.articleSummary: Mpox patient in Divinópolis, Centro-Oeste Minas Gerais, found after leaving the Hospital Universitário, abandoning treatment and isolation. The 36-year-old man was located in the Niterói neighborhood. Social outreach teams ensured continuity of care and protection of public health. The municipality said he has characteristics compatible with mpox, requiring preventive and transmission-control measures even without lab confirmation. Mpox is a notifiable infectious disease requiring medical follow-up and isolation during the transmission period; transmission occurs through direct contact with skin lesions, secretions, and contaminated objects. Noncompliance with sanitary measures to prevent the spread of contagious diseases can constitute a crime under Article 268 of the Brazilian Penal Code, with penalties up to one year in detention and fines.

triage.headline_ja: 隔離を離脱したMpox患者、ディヴィノーポリスで発見される
triage.triage_reason: 単一患者の隔離離脱事例であり、ラボ確認もない個別症例報告で、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響や国際的拡大の懸念は認められない。
triage.notes: ラボ確認前の単一症例であり、個人の隔離違反という社会的・法的側面が主題。公衆衛生危機としての規模は確認されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Casos prováveis de dengue sobem 120% em SC e secretário alerta para 'temporada muito pesada' com El Niño
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Probable dengue cases rise 120% in Santa Catarina, and the secretary warns of a "very heavy season" with El Niño.
article.articleSummary: Probable dengue cases in Santa Catarina, Brazil surged about 120% in the first three weeks of November 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, totaling 727 cases vs 331. From January 1 to November 25, 2026, the state reported 3,838 probable dengue cases and 1,587 confirmed, with no deaths. Health officials warn that El Niño could trigger a very heavy transmission season due to increased Aedes aegypti proliferation. Prevention emphasis targets households and communities, including eliminating standing water, securing water tanks, cleaning gutters and drains, maintaining treated pools, and inspecting homes during vector-control visits. Common dengue symptoms include high fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgias/arthralgias, nausea, fatigue, and red skin rashes; seek urgent care for severe signs such as intense abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, dizziness, bleeding, breathing difficulties, or fainting. Continuous prevention and community participation remain crucial.

triage.headline_ja: サンタカタリーナ州でデング熱の疑い例が120%増加、エルニーニョで「非常に厳しいシーズン」になると長官が警告
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル国内の季節的なデング熱増加であり、死亡例なし・国際的拡大の兆候もないが、エルニーニョによる媒介蚊増殖で感染拡大の可能性があるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: デング熱はブラジルで毎年流行する風土病であり、今回は季節的増加の報道。死亡例なしで重症度は低いが、エルニーニョによる媒介蚊増殖のため今後の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Bahia registra 19 casos de mpox em 2026; Salvador concentra maioria dos diagnósticos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bahia records 19 mpox cases in 2026; Salvador accounts for the majority of diagnoses.
article.articleSummary: Bahia state reported 19 monkeypox (mpox) cases in 2026, with Salvador de Bahia accounting for 12 diagnoses. Other cases were in São Sebastião do Passé (2), Feira de Santana (1), São Francisco do Conde (1), and Vitória da Conquista (1); two patients live in other states. Epidemiological Surveillance notes that a resident’s location does not necessarily reflect where infection occurred. The agency stresses continued surveillance, early diagnosis, and preventive measures, especially during peak tourist periods and large events. Mpox is caused by the mpox virus (MPXV) and spreads mainly via direct contact with lesions, mucous membranes, or secretions of infected individuals, as well as through contaminated objects and close, prolonged interactions. Symptoms typically include fever, headache, muscle pains, lymphadenopathy, and skin or mucosal lesions, which can appear in genital or anal regions, potentially without other signs.

triage.headline_ja: バイーア州、2026年にmpox19症例を記録；サルバドールが診断の大半を占める
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・バイーア州でmpoxの散発的発生が継続しているが、症例数は限定的で重症度や国際的拡大の兆候は示されておらず、継続監視が妥当。
triage.notes: エルサルバドルは発生地域に含まれるが、記事はブラジル・バイーア州の国内症例報告が主題でありエルサルバドルでの発生は言及されていないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Nghệ An ghi nhận hơn 300 ca cúm A trong nửa tháng
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Nghe An records more than 300 influenza A cases in the past two weeks
article.articleSummary: Influenza A is surging in Nghệ An Province, Vietnam, with more than 300 influenza A cases treated in the first half of November at Nghệ An General Hospital; September had 59 cases, October 289, and early November pushed past 300. Patients typically present with headache, high fever, cough, muscle aches, and fatigue. Not all influenza A infections require hospitalization, but severe cases can progress to pneumonia or respiratory failure, prompting inpatient care for high‑risk individuals; similar patterns were recorded at Nghệ An Obstetrics and Pediatrics Hospital. In response to rising transmission, the Nghệ An Department of Health directed schools and local authorities to tighten prevention: regular cleaning and disinfection, adequate water and soap, well‑ventilated classrooms, daily health monitoring, and isolation of students with fever or cough. As of 26 November 2026, the province reports over 2,000 seasonal influenza cases with no deaths. Vaccination is urged for those aged 6 months and older, with priority for young children, seniors, pregnant women, and those with chronic or immunodeficiency conditions; continue hand hygiene and masking.

triage.headline_ja: ゲアン省、2週間で300例以上のインフルエンザA型患者を記録
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザの流行であり死亡例もなく、通常の公衆衛生対応の範囲内で国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザAの地域的増加で、死亡例なし。地方保健当局による学校・地域での予防対策強化が行われており、通常の季節性疾患管理の範囲内と判断。

article.articleHeadline: Thailand Urges Year-End Vigilance as Three Illnesses Spread
article.articleSummary: Thailand’s Department of Disease Control reports continued circulation of seasonal influenza (645,874 cases through Nov 15) and mpox (470 infections through Oct 31, three deaths in 2026), plus more than 130 combined diphtheria-pertussis cases in the far south with six deaths in the three southern border provinces. Cooler weather and heavy domestic travel ahead of New Year celebrations threaten to accelerate transmission. Infants, older adults and immunocompromised face higher risk; exposure varies by region. Influenza symptoms include abrupt high fever, body aches, chills, sore throat and fatigue. Pertussis starts like a cold then violent coughing; infants may have apnea. Mpox presents with fever, headache, lymphadenopathy, and skin lesions; some cases have few lesions or no fever; PCR of skin lesions is required. Prevention emphasizes free annual flu vaccines for high-risk groups, pertussis boosters for pregnant women and children, hand hygiene, masks, and prompt care for fever, breathing trouble, or rash.

triage.headline_ja: タイ、年末に向け3つの感染症拡大への警戒を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザ・サル痘・南部でのジフテリア百日咳混合流行（死亡6名）が報告されているが、いずれも既知の疾患で国際的拡大の兆候はなく、タイ政府による定例的な注意喚起に近いため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 複数疾患（インフルエンザ、Mpox、ジフテリア・百日咳）が同時に報告されているが、いずれもタイ国内の既知の流行パターンであり、年末年始の人流増加に伴う注意喚起が主目的。南部国境3県でのジフテリア・百日咳混合流行（死亡6名）は注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Alerta sanitário na Zona da Mata: Juiz de Fora confirma mais de 40 casos de Covid-19 em 13 dias e investiga duas mortes; Palma também registra alta
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Public health alert in the Zona da Mata region: Juiz de Fora confirms more than 40 COVID-19 cases in 13 days and investigates two deaths; Palma also records an increase.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 resurgence in Zona da Mata, Minas Gerais: Juiz de Fora reports 44 new confirmed cases in 13 days (Nov 12–25, 2026), lifting November to a yearly high with 153 cases in 2026 to date. Two deaths under epidemiological investigation: a 62-year-old woman at UPA São Pedro and a 95-year-old man at Regional Leste tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 but had severe preexisting conditions. Palma records 13 confirmed cases between Nov 18–23, 2026, all mild and non-hospitalized. Testing supply is strained; rapid tests await a new shipment; RT-PCR remains available for SRAG. Vaccination update: 6,000 doses of the updated vaccine received; priority groups include children 6 months–<5 years, pregnant people, 60+, and those with comorbidities; 30,693 doses administered in Juiz de Fora Jan–Nov 23, 2026. Guidance emphasizes vaccination, ventilation, masking, and prompt care for respiratory symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: ゾナ・ダ・マタ地区で公衆衛生警報：ジュイス・デ・フォーラが13日間で40件以上のCOVID-19症例を確認、2件の死亡を調査中；パルマでも増加を記録
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19の季節的な地域的増加であり、既存の監視体制内で管理されている通常の事象。国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: COVID-19は既知の疾患であり、ブラジル国内の一地域での季節的な症例増加。死亡例は高齢・基礎疾患保有者で、ワクチン接種体制も機能している。

article.articleHeadline: Crato realiza Dia D de Multivacinação e vacinação contra a dengue neste sábado (28) - Portal M1
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Crato Holds D-Day for Multivaccination and Dengue Vaccination This Saturday (28) - Portal M1.
article.articleSummary: Crato, Brazil launches a D-Day of Multivaccination and dengue vaccination on Saturday, November 28, 2026, from 08:00 to 12:00 at Family Health Units (USFs) citywide. The Crato City Hall, via the Municipal Health Secretariat, aims to expand vaccine access, update residents’ immunization records, and provide dengue vaccination at participating sites. Attendees can review their vaccination cards and receive doses indicated by the national immunization calendar. Participating USFs include Nossa Senhora de Fátima I and II; José Pinheiro Esmeraldo (Muriti III); Marta Nascimento da Silva (Pantanal); Madre Feitosa; Vicência Garrido (Muriti II); Sertãozinho; José Wellington Luiz de Sousa (Dom Quintino); Centro; Verônica Maria Couto Pinheiro (Belmonte); Centro de Nutrição de Crato; Muriti (Muriti I); Palmereval; Fábio Pinheiro Esmeraldo; and Tarcísio Pinheiro (São Miguel). The event emphasizes dengue prevention and routine vaccination catch-up for Crato residents.

triage.headline_ja: クラト市、11月28日(土)にワクチン一斉接種デーとデング熱ワクチン接種を実施 - Portal M1
triage.triage_reason: これはデング熱の予防接種キャンペーンに関する行政広報記事であり、アウトブレイクや異常な公衆衛生事象を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は定期的なワクチン接種イベントの告知であり、感染症の発生・流行を報告するものではないため対象国への計上は行わない。

article.articleHeadline: Lambayeque supera los 20,600 casos de dengue y reporta 45 fallecidos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lambayeque surpasses 20,600 dengue cases and reports 45 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Dengue in Lambayeque, Peru, totals 20,634 accumulated cases and 45 deaths through epidemiological week 47. Cases include arrivals from Bagua (Amazonas), Rioja (San Martín), Jaén (Cajamarca) and Trujillo (La Libertad) due to patient mobility. Most infections have confirmed diagnoses; some tests remain under evaluation. Of the 45 deaths, 27 are women and 18 men; the 60+ age group bears the highest mortality. Districts with the highest incidence are Chiclayo, José Leonardo Ortiz, Reque, Lagunas, Cayaltí, La Victoria, Motupe and Olmos. More than 40 brigades are conducting home interventions; eight clinical surveillance units operate across three provinces and 48 fever units across 38 districts to assess cases and refer severe patients. Vaccination reaches 61% (32,666 doses) as of Nov 18, with second doses underway in Chiclayo, La Victoria, Motupe. El Niño–related conditions may boost transmission; sustain vector control and community prevention, including eliminating water containers and seeking medical care for dengue symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: ランバイェケ州のデング熱感染者が20,600人を超え、45人の死亡を報告
triage.triage_reason: デング熱による死亡者45人、感染者2万人超という大規模アウトブレイクであり、重症度・持続的曝露・流行性の観点から懸念が高い。政府による大規模な対応（予防接種、監視班配置）も確認される。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はペルー・ランバイェケ州のデング熱流行であり、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空配列とした。発生地域にブラジル・ベネズエラが含まれるが記事本文では言及されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Por que o Brasil vive surto de mpox? O que se sabe -- e o que não se sabe -- sobre os novos casos da doença
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Why is Brazil experiencing an mpox outbreak? What is known—and what is not known—about the new cases of the disease.
article.articleSummary: Brazil’s mpox outbreak is linked to clade 1b, DR Congo lineage that emerged in 2023 and spread by 2024. While studies are lacking, evidence suggests clade 1b predominance among recent cases. Although clade 1 has been linked to more lesions, severity and fatality with clade 1b appear similar to clade 2b; outcomes depend on age, immune status, and access to care. The surge is centered in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, likely due to population size and connectivity. Transmission remains through close contact and sexual activity, with MSM accounting for about 93% of diagnoses outside Africa (Sept 2025–2026) and 96% via sexual contact. Hospitalizations ~13.6%; one death this year among the immunocompromised. Compared with 2022’s 10,591 cases and 14 deaths, 2026 has 1,499 cases and 1 death. Brazil has 25,000 vaccine doses (US$65 per dose, two doses) aimed at high-risk groups; vaccination alone is not sufficient.

triage.headline_ja: なぜブラジルはmpoxの流行に見舞われているのか？新規症例について分かっていること、分かっていないこと
triage.triage_reason: ブラジルでより重症度が高いとされるclade 1b（DRC系統）による症例が拡大しており、死亡例・入院例も確認されていることから、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し、公衆衛生上の懸念が高い。
triage.notes: DRC（clade 1bの起源）はイベント発生国ではなく系統の由来として言及されているのみのため、verified_locationsには含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Lagos unveils digital Bioshield to tackle emerging disease threats
article.articleSummary: Lagos State unveiled the Lagos State Bioshield, a biosecurity system powered by AI and telemedicine to detect and contain disease threats while keeping economic activity going. The framework screens entry risks and tracks symptomatic arrivals via Health Radar, using WhatsApp, SMS and email to register travellers and participants and conduct 21-day health checks. Symptomatic individuals receive telemedicine assessments with laboratory investigations and referrals. Deployed at CANEX WKND, the system monitored 19,000 delegates, including 2,298 visitors, with 2,454 telemedicine consultations, 241 clinical referrals and 219 flags for follow-up; all cases closed with no severe outcomes. Lagos, population 30.1 million, faces high density and reliance on earnings; it handles 70% of Nigeria’s international air traffic and 1.8 million cattle annually, underscoring One Health needs. Threats include Lassa fever, dengue, yellow fever, Marburg, Ebola and emerging pathogens. Bioshield 3.0 planned; calls for Africa-wide BioShield Alliance among megacities Lagos, Cairo, Kinshasa, Johannesburg and Nairobi.

triage.headline_ja: ラゴス州、新興感染症脅威に対処するためデジタルBioshieldを発表
triage.triage_reason: 特定の疾病アウトブレイクの報告ではなく、ナイジェリア・ラゴス州の監視システム導入に関する一般的な取り組み紹介記事であり、対象国（本リストの11か国）での発生も確認できない。

article.articleHeadline: BMKG Rilis Peringatan Dini Cuaca Lampung, Kenali Gejala Leptospirosis yang Mirip Flu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: BMKG Releases Early Weather Warning for Lampung; Know the Symptoms of Leptospirosis That Resemble Flu.
article.articleSummary: On 26 November 2026, BMKG issued an early weather warning for Lampung, Indonesia, citing heavy rainfall and flood risks that raise leptospirosis exposure. Leptospirosis is a bacterial zoonosis caused by Leptospira interrogans, transmitted via urine or blood of infected animals and common in tropical regions during flooding. Bacteria persist for months to years in animal kidneys and contaminate water or soil. Infection occurs through skin contact with contaminated water or soil, or ingestion. At-risk groups include outdoor workers (farmers, fishermen, miners), animal handlers, sanitation workers, flood-prone residents, and recreational water users. Symptoms appear 2 days to 4 weeks post-infection and resemble flu or dengue: high fever, chills, nausea, muscle pain, and rash; some progress to Weil disease requiring hospitalization. Diagnosis uses ELISA/rapid tests, PCR, MAT; treatment ranges from supportive care to IV antibiotics for organ involvement. Prevention emphasizes protective gear, wound care, safe water, and animal vaccination. Monitor updates via BMKG.

article.articleHeadline: Dengue: reportaron 11 casos importados en Argentina durante la temporada 2026-2027
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue: 11 imported cases reported in Argentina during the 2026–2027 season.
article.articleSummary: Dengue: 11 imported dengue cases reported in Argentina for the 2026–2027 season. In detail, Córdoba records two cases and Santa Fe one, all with travel history to Peru, and Santa Cruz reports another case after visiting Costa Rica. Across Argentina, 1,584 suspected dengue cases have been tallied, with 797 discarded, 760 under investigation, and 16 classified as probable. The first two imported Córdoba cases have been confirmed. Chikungunya: no new locally acquired cases in the latest week; one imported case detected in Salta’s Orán department, with travel history to Bolivia. Overall transmission risk remains low, but the NOA outbreak underscores the need for active surveillance, particularly to identify acute fever patients without diagnosis and to detect potential new transmission foci early.

article.articleHeadline: São Paulo anuncia o fim do surto de sarampo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: São Paulo Announces the End of the Measles Outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreak in São Paulo ends after 12 weeks with no new infections linked to identified transmission chains. In 2026, 41 cases were recorded in the state: 37 in the capital (São Paulo city), 2 in São Bernardo do Campo, 1 in Guarulhos, and 1 in Santo André; all patients recovered. Last confirmed case had symptom onset on August 28. Surveillance continues with ongoing investigation of suspected cases and contact tracing, alongside emphasis on vaccination uptake. September first-dose coverage of the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine reached 96.9% in the state, above the 95% target, while second-dose coverage remained below ideal at 84.85%. Individuals without a complete vaccination schedule, those unsure of their vaccination status, or who misplaced records should seek health services to update vaccination. Vigilance and vaccination efforts are ongoing to prevent resurgence.

article.articleHeadline: Temperatura e acidez podem facilitar entrada do vírus da dengue nas células
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Temperature and acidity may facilitate entry of the dengue virus into cells.
article.articleSummary: Dengue virus envelope protein E dimers from DENV-2 and DENV-3 are studied by Unesp in São José do Rio Preto, with the Italian Institute of Technology, using dynamic molecular simulations. Analyzing the E-dimer at 28°C, 37°C, and 40°C and at pH 7, 6, 5, researchers find that warming from mosquito to human temperature weakens inter-dimer contacts, an effect amplified by acidity, promoting conformational changes that expose the fusion region and enable entry. At 40°C, some connections re-close, not simply more disruption. DENV-2 shows greater destabilization at pH 5; DENV-3 shows notable changes at pH 6. The study describes a compensatory embrace where one half of the dimer opens while the other remains bound, altering fusion-loop exposure and potentially antibody recognition. Mapping hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, and ionic interactions reveals targets to reinforce dimer linkage and block pH-triggered fusion. Brazil remains a dengue-priority public health issue; 2025 reports ~1.7 million probable cases and ~1,800 deaths; through Oct 2026: ~490,000 cases and ~370 deaths.

article.articleHeadline: Ébola avanza en El Congo con 11 mil 700 casos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola advances in Congo with 11,700 cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola Bundibugyo advances in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with 11,793 confirmed cases and 5,779 deaths across numerous health zones, case fatality about 49%. The outbreak, centered in Ituri and North Kivu in the northeast, progresses more slowly than Zaire Ebola, with early symptoms like fever, fatigue and muscle pains, delaying recognition and isolation. There is no approved vaccine or licensed antivirals for Bundibugyo; candidates such as the rVSV Bundibugyo vaccine and remdesivir are in trials, not ready for widespread use. Only about 11% of cases come from contact-tracing lists; the rest are detected outside surveillance. Two-thirds of deaths occur in community settings due to home care and traditional burials, amid conflict, displacement, poverty, and malnutrition that hinder response. Cross-border spread: imported cases identified in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria and France; Uganda declared its outbreak over in July; France contained a single imported case.
